If it were ever constructed, From<CommandError>'s catch-all arm ('_ => OperationFailure::Generic(err.to_string())', event.rs:1284) would carry that string into PackageEvent::Completed and thence to both the CLI display and the MCP JSON.

This is the one place where .claude/rules/secrets.md's guidance — 'use to_string(), never {:?}' — would NOT be sufficient, because the leak is in Display rather than Debug. Every other CommandError variant's #[error(...)] omits stdout, which is what makes that rule safe elsewhere.

Unreachable today, so not a live exposure. But it is a loaded gun in a match arm designed to be a safe fallback. Either delete the variant, or bound its Display, before streaming ever grows an error path that constructs it.

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-ppp.
acceptance_criteria: CommandError::Callback is removed, or its Display cannot emit unbounded command output.

title: CheckResult carries a check command's stdout and the CLI prints it
description:
CheckResult::Failed and CheckResult::Success carry the check command's stdout, and the CLI prints it at crates/cli/src/commands/package/check.rs:139-149 and :190-210. MCP is unaffected — it renders a label only.

Same class as selfie-ppp (a user-defined command's output reaching a display verbatim) but a different type and a different display path, so selfie-ppp's fix to CommandFailure::ExecutionFailed does not cover it. Notably this one is NOT gated on the multi-error summary's two-error threshold, so it surfaces on a single failing check.

Found while tracing every exit for selfie-ppp; held out of that unit's scope deliberately.

When fixing, apply the same policy selfie-ppp establishes rather than inventing a second one: a user-defined command's stdout is content selfie does not control and may be a credential; stderr may be forwarded truncated on failure.
acceptance_criteria: A check command's stdout is not surfaced verbatim by default, consistent with whatever policy selfie-ppp establishes.

title: Decide whether test-lib belongs in just check and the CLAUDE.md checklist
description:
PR #70 added a CI step running 'cargo test -p selfie' alone, because every workspace-wide command unifies the with_mocks feature in from another crate's dev-dependencies and so cannot catch the library losing access to it.

That gate now exists in three places with three different answers:
- .github/workflows/ci.yml runs it as its own step. Yes.
- Justfile has it as 'test-lib' but 'just check' does NOT include it.
- CLAUDE.md's pre-commit checklist is four steps and does not mention it.

selfie-blkr makes the pre-commit-check skill run 'just check' AND 'just test-lib', which closes the gap for agents using the skill but makes the skill a SUPERSET of the documented checklist — a human running 'just check' or following CLAUDE.md still misses it. That is a smaller, deliberately-created drift, flagged rather than hidden by the author of that fix.

Decide the single answer: either add test-lib to 'just check' and make CLAUDE.md's checklist five steps (so every path covers it), or record that it is CI's job alone and remove it from the skill. The current three-way split is what produced selfie-blkr in the first place.

Note the cost side: 'just check' already runs the workspace suite, so adding test-lib means one extra compile of selfie at a different feature set. Measured on this machine it is a few seconds warm.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p selfie is either in every local gate path or explicitly documented as CI-only, not present in some and absent from others.
notes:
ANSWER REVISED 2026-07-29 by the maintainer, superseding the earlier 'add it to the checklist' decision.

The question was wrong-shaped. 'Where should test-lib live?' assumes a hand-picked crate+feature combination is the right instrument. It is not. Verified: selfie is the ONLY crate in the workspace with an optional feature (with_mocks = ["mockall"]; mockall is the only optional=true dependency anywhere), and selfie-cli / selfie-mcp / test-common have no [features] section at all. So isolating any other crate would catch nothing, and isolating selfie covers exactly one combination.

RESOLUTION: cargo-hack in CI, replacing the ad-hoc 'Test the library crate alone' step PR #70 added:
    cargo hack --each-feature test -p selfie
and REMOVE test-lib from CLAUDE.md's pre-commit checklist entirely. The break this guards against (test-common dropping its features request) can only reach main through a PR, and CI gates PRs — a pre-commit step is the wrong layer.

Why this is better than what it replaces: it covers every feature combination rather than the single one the workspace run happens to produce, and it generalizes. Add a second optional feature later and cargo-hack covers the combinations automatically, whereas a hand-picked test-lib step would silently under-test and nobody would notice.

Being implemented in the selfie-blkr PR; close against that.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #73 (merged d9bb7f9).

selfie-blkr: the pre-commit-check skill was DELETED rather than corrected. It duplicated a checklist CLAUDE.md already carries and already loads every session, and that duplication is what let the two drift apart. CLAUDE.md's checklist now delegates to 'just check', so no second copy of the commands exists to weaken. Premise verified empirically rather than restated: on an isolated copy with a planted clippy::needless_return, 'cargo clippy --all-targets' exits 0 while printing the warning and '-- -D warnings' exits 101 on identical code.

selfie-it6l: resolved differently than the bead framed it. The question assumed a hand-picked crate+feature invocation was the right instrument. selfie is the only crate in the workspace with an optional feature (with_mocks; mockall is the only optional=true dependency), so it was the only crate worth isolating and nothing said why. CI now runs 'cargo hack --each-feature test -p selfie', covering all four combinations instead of the one the workspace run produces, and extending itself if a second feature appears. Removed from the local checklist: the break can only reach main through a PR, and CI gates PRs. Verified the replacement is a strict superset — deleting test-common's features line fails cargo-hack on pass 2 of 4 with the predicted from_parts error, and the old gate exits 101 on the same mutation.

selfie-cm1h: the trailing sentence was retensed and its citation historicized rather than deleted, so it still explains why obsolete '--features with_mocks' instructions exist elsewhere. Worth recording why this was more than a P4 nit: THREE independent agents misread that sentence during this batch — one reported CLAUDE.md as stale, one claimed 'just test-lib' would fail every time and cited it as proof, one filed it as a stale-docs finding on an unrelated PR. All three were wrong. The mechanism, diagnosed by the selfie-ppp author, is that all three misread a TRAILING CLAUSE qualifying an earlier claim; a reader who stops at the first assertion gets the opposite meaning. The fix leads with 'The command compiles today.' as a standalone sentence.

title: The typos pre-commit hook may not affect the commit it fires on
description:
A PreToolUse hook in .claude/settings.json runs 'typos --write-changes' before any 'git commit'. It EDITS FILES ON DISK, which means whether the fix reaches the commit depends on how the commit is made:

- Agent stages first, then runs a plain 'git commit': the commit takes the INDEX, which was built before the hook rewrote the working tree. The typo fix stays unstaged and CI's check-typos job still fails — the hook did work, silently, for nothing.
- Agent runs 'git commit -- <paths>': the paths are re-read from the working tree at commit time, so the fix lands.

So the hook is effective on one commit path and silently ineffective on the other. .claude/rules/verification.md recommends 'git commit -- <paths>' (for unrelated staging-safety reasons), which happens to be the path where the hook works — so the failure may be masked in practice by a convention adopted for a different purpose. That is a fragile reason for a hook to function.

Stated as a mechanism by the author of selfie-blkr from reading the hook, NOT as a tested observation. Confirm it before fixing: stage a file containing a typo, run a plain 'git commit', and check whether the committed blob carries the fix.

If confirmed, options: have the hook re-stage what it changed ('git add -u' on the affected paths), or make it a check that BLOCKS the commit rather than a silent rewrite, so the agent is told rather than having its commit quietly diverge from its working tree.
acceptance_criteria: The typos hook either affects every commit path it fires on, or blocks the commit so the discrepancy cannot be silent.
notes:
FRAMING SHARPENED by the final reviewer on selfie-blkr. The mechanism as filed is correct, but the finding is worse than 'the hook sometimes does nothing':

.claude/rules/verification.md PRESCRIBES 'git commit -- <paths>' as the preferred commit form (for unrelated staging-safety reasons). That is precisely the form under which the hook's rewrite DOES reach the commit — meaning the repo's own recommended convention is the one that commits hook-edited content the author never reviewed or staged. The plain-git-commit path, where the fix is silently dropped, is the one the convention steers people away from.

So both branches are wrong in opposite directions: the discouraged path silently discards the fix, and the recommended path silently includes an unreviewed edit. Neither tells the author anything. That argues for making the hook BLOCK with a message rather than rewrite, since the failure is silence in both directions rather than a missing re-stage.

title: A live plan doc prescribes the bare clippy form as its per-step gate
description:
docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-24-provider-sourced-dotfiles.md prescribes 'cargo clippy --all-targets' with no '-- -D warnings' at roughly ten places (:25, :202, :387, :564, :741, :1041, :1182, :1240, :1307, :1317), and :25 labels it '(zero warnings)' — the exact mislabel selfie-blkr fixes in the pre-commit-check skill.

This one matters more than the others because it is LIVE: the plan is dated 2026-07-24, it covers provider-sourced dotfiles, and agents have been working in that area since. An agent executing the plan step by step runs the under-reporting gate at every checkpoint and can ship a warning to a red CI while believing each step passed.

Older documents carry the same text but are archival records of completed work rather than instructions anyone will follow: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-15-streaming-package-list.md:346,375; docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-20-config-file-deployment.md (about 12 occurrences); and three specs. Fixing the live plan is the point; the archival ones are a low-priority sweep and arguably should be left as the historical record of what was actually run.

Note these files are local-excluded working artifacts per project convention, so 'fixing' them may mean fixing the template or habit that produces them rather than the files themselves.

Found by the author of selfie-blkr.
acceptance_criteria: The live plan doc prescribes the CI clippy form, or plan docs stop prescribing gate commands inline.
notes: UNDERCOUNTED at filing. The final reviewer on selfie-blkr found docs/superpowers/plans/2026-03-20-config-file-deployment.md carries 14 MORE bare 'cargo clippy --all-targets' occurrences (lines 275, 370, 471, 692, 765, 924, 1010, 1137, 1168, 1224, 1265, 1368, 1425 and following), on top of the ten in the 2026-07-24 provider-sourced-dotfiles plan. Also: BOTH line 25 and line 1317 of the 07-24 plan mislabel it '(zero warnings)', not just line 25.

title: TILT.md documents 14 just targets that do not exist
description:
TILT.md (last touched 2026-03-16) references 17 'just' invocations. 'just --list' shows the Justfile provides only: build, check, clippy, default, docs, fmt, fmt-check, outdated, test, test-cli, test-lib.

Of TILT.md's references, only 'just build', 'just docs' and 'just fmt' exist. These do not:
  just docker build-images / clean / logs / rebuild-images / shell-alpine / shell-debian / start / status / stop
  just local-clippy
  just local-test
  just tilt test / test-alpine / test-debian

Anyone following TILT.md gets 'error: Justfile does not contain recipe' on nearly every command in it. There is exactly one Justfile in the repo (confirmed by find; no submodule Justfiles), so this is not a path problem.

Two notes. First, 'just local-clippy' is additionally the weaker-gate flavor of selfie-blkr — whatever it once ran, a name like that suggests a local variant of the clippy gate, which is the pattern that under-reports. Second, the doc looks broadly stale rather than wrong in one line, so the fix is probably to rewrite or delete it rather than patch names; decide whether the Tilt/Docker workflow it describes still exists at all before restoring any of it.

Found by the author of selfie-blkr while checking whether the same defect appeared elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: TILT.md describes commands that exist, or is removed if the workflow it documents no longer does.

title: track-dotfile strands the copied source file when the package save fails
description:
crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:1607 copies the user's dotfile into the package directory, then :1619 calls save_package. If the save fails, the copied file is left behind with no cleanup.

Measured on the selfie-6lz4 branch, where the new save guard makes this reachable: 'selfie package track-dotfile' on a package carrying an unrecognized key refuses the save, leaves '.newfile' in packages/<name>/, and a retry after fixing the typo then fails with 'Source file already exists at .../creds/.newfile. Remove it first or choose a different file.' The user must manually delete a file they never knowingly created.

Pre-existing ordering — ANY save_package failure (permissions, disk full, serialization error) does this. selfie-6lz4 amplifies it by adding a new and quite reachable failure mode rather than creating it.

Fix: copy after a successful save, or remove the copied file on the save-failure path. The first is better if nothing in the save depends on the file already being present — check that before choosing.

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-6lz4.
acceptance_criteria: A failed package save during track-dotfile leaves no copied source file behind.

title: The non-unix arms of write_file_no_follow and write_file_private are built by no CI job
description:
crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:141-155 is the #[cfg(not(unix))] arm of write_file_no_follow — a racy symlink_metadata fallback, including deliberate handling for 'a stat that fails for any reason other than absent is an error'. Every job in .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on ubuntu-latest, so that branch has never been compiled, let alone run, anywhere. The same is true of the Windows arm of write_file_private.

The comments on those branches are careful and appear correct. They are simply unverified: a syntax error, a type error, or an inverted condition would not be caught by anything. Code that cannot fail a build is code nobody has checked.

This is a standing repo-wide gap rather than something selfie-4m9 introduced — noting it there only because that change added a second such branch on a security-relevant write path, where an untested fallback is worse than elsewhere.

Options: add a windows-latest (and/or macos-latest) job to CI so the arms at least compile; or, if non-unix is not actually supported, say so and make the arms a compile_error! rather than a plausible-looking implementation that has never run. The second is cheaper and more honest if nobody is running selfie on Windows.

Found by the final reviewer on selfie-4m9.
acceptance_criteria: Every platform arm of the filesystem writers is either compiled by CI or replaced with an explicit refusal to support that platform.

title: save_package shells out to dprint from inside the selfie library
description:
crates/selfie/src/package/repository/yaml.rs:250-270: YamlPackageRepository::save_package spawns 'dprint fmt' on the file it just wrote, with a 5-second poll-and-kill loop.

Two problems.

First, it is a boundary violation in spirit. The selfie library is supposed to be frontend-agnostic — CLAUDE.md says it should not assume it is called from a CLI, and .claude/rules/architecture.md routes all outward effects through the event system. Shelling out to a developer-machine code formatter is an undeclared dependency on the caller's PATH and on a tool that has nothing to do with the domain. An MCP server, a GUI, or a test harness on a machine without dprint gets different behavior with no signal (it is silently skipped).

Second, the poll-and-kill loop is a hand-rolled timeout in a library that already has a CommandRunner port with timeout handling. If formatting saved files is genuinely desired, it belongs in the adapter that knows a developer is present, or behind the existing port.

Pre-existing; found by the final reviewer on selfie-6lz4 while tracing save_package for an unrelated fail-open.
acceptance_criteria: Saved package formatting either moves out of the library or goes through an existing port, rather than the library spawning dprint directly.

title: Decide and record whether the two dotfile writers should keep diverging on symlinks
description:
After selfie-4m9 selfie has two write paths that treat a symlinked target OPPOSITELY:

- Repository-file dotfiles: REFUSE (O_NOFOLLOW), warn, skip. Rationale: the user's symlink is legitimate config, the content is recoverable, and destroying the link on a routine unprompted update was measured to be the default path, not an edge case.
- Secret/provider-sourced dotfiles: REPLACE the link atomically. Rationale: a credential must never reach an attacker-chosen destination, and replacement is the only safe way to COMPLETE the write.

Both are correct in isolation and each is documented on its own side. But the divergence is currently an emergent consequence of two separately-reasoned decisions, not a recorded one, and nothing states that they SHOULD differ. The next person to notice will read it as an inconsistency and 'fix' it — in whichever direction they happen to be standing.

This is ADR material rather than a bug: state the two behaviors, the reason each is right for its content type, and that unifying them would be wrong. Per the project's ADR conventions the document must be timeless and maintainer-facing, with no bead IDs or plan narrative.

Raised by the author of selfie-4m9 as something needing a deliberate decision rather than a silent divergence.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR records why repository-file and secret dotfile writers differ on symlinked targets, and that the difference is intentional.

title: MCP tool descriptions still promise auto_accept=true always overwrites
description:
crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs:176 and :594 describe auto_accept=true as forcing an overwrite of the target. After selfie-4m9 that is no longer unconditionally true: a symlinked target is refused regardless of auto_accept, because the refusal is enforced by the kernel at the write (O_NOFOLLOW) and is not a confirmation prompt that auto_accept can answer.

The MCP tool description is the AI assistant's entire contract for what the tool does — it has no other source of truth and cannot read the Rust. A description promising unconditional overwrite will produce assistants that confidently tell users their file was overwritten when it was skipped.

Left untouched by selfie-4m9 deliberately: it is the sibling adapter's user-facing text and out of that unit's scope.

Fix: state the exception in both descriptions. While there, check whether any other MCP description promises behavior that selfie-4m9 changed.
acceptance_criteria: No MCP tool description promises an overwrite that a symlinked target will not receive.

title: A dotfile target that is a fifo or device node hangs or writes to the device
description:
fs::write to a fifo blocks forever waiting for a reader, so a dotfile target that is a named pipe hangs 'selfie apply' indefinitely. command_timeout does not bound it — that governs provider commands, not filesystem writes. A character or block device node would be written to directly.

selfie-4m9's O_NOFOLLOW guard does NOT close this: O_NOFOLLOW refuses a symlink at the final component and nothing else. Opening a fifo O_WRONLY still blocks; opening a device still succeeds.

Pre-existing and not introduced by selfie-4m9, but adjacent enough to note there: the reviewer raised it while deciding what perform_deploy should do for non-regular targets, and the answer 'refuse anything that is not a regular file or absent' would close both this and part of selfie-4m9 with one check.

Suggested direction: stat the target with symlink_metadata before writing and refuse anything that is neither absent nor a regular file, with a warning naming what was found. Note this is a check-then-write and so racy on its own — it is a usability guard against a user's own odd filesystem, not a security boundary; the security boundary for symlinks is O_NOFOLLOW in the open itself.

Found by the plan reviewer on selfie-4m9.
acceptance_criteria: A dotfile target that is a fifo, socket or device node is refused with a diagnostic rather than hanging or being written to.

title: Three more write sites follow symlinks the same way perform_deploy did
description:
selfie-4m9 fixes the symlink-following write at perform_deploy. The identical mechanism remains at three other sites, all still using FileSystem::write_file (fs::write), which follows a symlink at the final path component:

- crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:1481 and :1607 — the track path, copying the user's existing dotfile INTO the packages/dotfiles repo.
- crates/selfie/src/package/repository/yaml.rs:249 — save_package, writing package YAML.

Each is preceded by a path_exists check, which FOLLOWS symlinks. So a DANGLING symlink planted at the destination passes the existence check (path_exists returns false) and fs::write then creates a file at the planter's chosen path. Same shape as the selfie-4m9 dangling-symlink repro.

Severity is lower than selfie-4m9: exploiting these requires write access to the user's package directory, and an attacker with that access can edit the package YAML directly for an easier win. The direction is also inward (into the repo) rather than outward to an arbitrary target.

Worth fixing for consistency rather than urgency — shipping 'selfie never writes through a symlink' while three sites still do is the kind of partial invariant that gets mistaken for a complete one. Whatever primitive selfie-4m9 lands (O_NOFOLLOW refusal) should be reused here; note the track path may want different semantics, since refusing to copy a file into the repo is a different user-facing outcome than refusing to deploy one out.

Found by the plan reviewer on selfie-4m9; scoped out deliberately to keep the P1 diff reviewable. Confirmed with the maintainer 2026-07-29.
acceptance_criteria: No FileSystem::write_file call site can write through a symlink at the final path component, or each remaining one is documented as deliberate.

title: Allow a dotfile entry to opt into following a symlinked target
description:
selfie-4m9 makes deploy REFUSE a symlinked target by default (O_NOFOLLOW; the write fails with ELOOP, a warning names the target and the link destination, and the entry is skipped). That is the right default: a symlink planted at a target otherwise redirects written content to a path the planter chose.

But a user who deliberately symlinks a config file into place — the stow-style workflow — now gets a warning and a skipped deploy with no supported way to say 'yes, I meant that'. Their dotfile silently stops updating until they remove the link.

Add an opt-in so an entry can follow through a symlink deliberately. Open questions that are the substance of this issue:
- Per-entry field in the package YAML, or a config-level setting, or both?
- Must it be FORBIDDEN on secret-bearing entries? A credential written through an attacker-controlled link is exactly the hole ADR-0003 closes, and a knob that reintroduces it by configuration is worse than no knob. Leaning yes: forbid it wherever the entry resolves to a secret-bearing content source, enforced at validation.
- Following a symlink safely still needs care: O_NOFOLLOW off means the write follows, so the opt-in should probably resolve the link explicitly and write to the resolved path, rather than merely disabling the guard.
- docs/package-files.md needs the field plus a plain statement of what the risk is.

Deferred deliberately from selfie-4m9 so the P1 ships as a small, reviewable, fail-closed change. Confirmed with the maintainer 2026-07-29: default refuse now, opt-in as follow-up. Note that all 8 dotfile targets tracked on the maintainer's own machine are regular files today, so nothing is broken in the meantime.
acceptance_criteria: A dotfile entry can opt into following a symlinked target; the option is refused or rejected for secret-bearing entries; behavior is documented.

title: docs 'Validation Rules for Dotfiles' omits command, vars, and the exactly-one-source invariant
description:
docs/package-files.md 'Validation Rules for Dotfiles' (~line 725) documents rules for 'source' and 'target' only.

Undocumented: anything about 'command', anything about 'vars', and the 'exactly one of source or command' invariant that ContentSource::Invalid enforces at runtime. A user whose entry specifies both, or neither, gets it skipped at apply time with a warning, having had no documented rule to check against.

This gap widens with selfie-6lz4, which makes an entry carrying an unknown key resolve to ContentSource::Invalid and be skipped — another way to land in Invalid that the docs do not describe.

Found by the plan reviewer on selfie-6lz4.
acceptance_criteria: The dotfile validation rules section documents command, vars, and every condition that yields ContentSource::Invalid.

title: selfie's own tests are not self-sufficient without with_mocks, and 14 silently vanish when it is off
description:
Two coupled problems, measured by the plan reviewer on selfie-4b7 in cold copies.

1. SILENT TEST LOSS. crates/selfie/src/package/service/deps.rs:272 is gated '#[cfg(all(test, feature = "with_mocks"))]' — the only all(...) gate in the crate; every other test module uses any(test, ...) or bare cfg(test). With with_mocks off, that module vanishes and 'cargo test -p selfie' reports GREEN while running 379 lib tests instead of 393. Doctests drop 6 to 5 for the same reason (the MockFileSystem::mock_read_file doctest at fs/filesystem.rs:301). A green run that quietly tests 14 fewer things is the .claude/rules/testing.md failure mode exactly.

2. THE MOCK SURFACE IS GATED IN MORE PLACES THAN THE TRAITS. Making selfie's unit tests compile without the feature is not the two-line cfg_attr change it looks like. Beyond the two automock cfg_attr sites (fs/filesystem.rs:21, package/port.rs:31) there are four separate feature-only gates: fs.rs:8 and config.rs:8 and commands.rs:9 (the 'pub use Mock*' re-exports) and fs/filesystem.rs:294 (the impl block holding mock_read_file, mock_path_exists, mock_config_dir_ok, mock_expand_path, mock_config_file). Flipping only the two cfg_attr sites takes the failure from 16 errors to 55, because the type is generated but neither re-exported nor equipped with its helpers.

Today selfie's own unit tests compile only because crates/test-common (a dev-dependency of selfie) requests features = ["with_mocks"] for its own use of CommandOutput::from_parts, and resolver-3 unification turns the feature on as a side effect. That is a load-bearing accident.

Fix direction: decide whether selfie's unit tests should be self-sufficient under bare cfg(test). If yes, all six gates must move together AND deps.rs:272 must stop being feature-conditional, or the change trades a loud compile error for silent test loss. If no, document the coupling (selfie-4b7 does this) and make the silent-skip impossible by dropping the feature arm from deps.rs:272.

Deliberately excluded from selfie-4b7's scope, which is a documentation correction.
acceptance_criteria: Either selfie's unit tests compile under bare cfg(test) with all mock gates moved together, or deps.rs:272 no longer skips 14 tests silently when the feature is off.

title: A ~user/... dotfile target gets a diagnostic that contradicts itself
description:
expand_secret_target (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs, documented as intentional at :301-306) deliberately leaves the '~user/path' named-user form unexpanded. The unexpanded path then trips the absolute-path guard, so the user is told targets must be absolute or start with '~/' — for a path that visibly DOES start with '~'.

The refusal is correct; the message is the bug. It describes a rule the input appears to satisfy, so the user has no way to work out what is actually wrong.

Should say that the named-user form ('~user/...') is not supported and that only '~/' for the current user is, rather than restating a rule the path seems to meet.

Found while planning selfie-4m9.
acceptance_criteria: A '~user/...' target produces a diagnostic that names the named-user form as the unsupported thing.

title: raw_yaml can be left empty, silently disabling unknown-field detection
description:
Package::validate_unknown_fields (crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:195) opens with 'if self.raw_yaml.is_empty() { return vec![]; }'. Detection therefore silently no-ops wherever raw_yaml was not populated — no error, no warning, no failing test.

Only two sites set it: repository/yaml.rs:123 and sync_service/service.rs:647. PackageBuilder does not. Any future deserialization site that forgets loses unknown-field detection entirely with no signal, and any test built via PackageBuilder that asserts on unknown-field validation passes vacuously.

This is an invariant the code states but does not enforce, which .claude/rules/verification.md calls out specifically: 'An invariant you can state is not an invariant the code enforces... If it matters, make it a type, a guard in a shared module, or a compile error.'

Candidate fix: make raw_yaml a required constructor parameter (or wrap it in a type that cannot be defaulted) so a deserialization site cannot forget it.

Widened slightly by selfie-6lz4, which extends validate_unknown_fields to dotfiles entries and so puts more behavior behind the same silent guard.
acceptance_criteria: A deserialization site that fails to populate raw_yaml is caught by the compiler or by a failing test, rather than silently losing unknown-field detection.
notes: Widened by the final reviewer on selfie-6lz4: validate_unknown_fields returns vec![] when raw_yaml is empty OR UNPARSABLE, so top-level unknown keys go unreported in both cases. The dotfile-entry check added by selfie-6lz4 deliberately avoids this by reading unknown keys off the entries themselves rather than re-parsing raw_yaml — that approach is the model for fixing the top-level check, and it also makes validation work for programmatically built packages, which the top-level check still cannot do.

title: test_known_fields_matches_package_struct cannot see skip_serializing_if fields
description:
crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:1282 guards KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS against drift by serializing a Package and asserting every emitted key is in the const. It uses a single PackageBuilder fixture.

Fields carrying #[serde(skip_serializing_if = ...)] are suppressed when unset, so a single fixture can never emit them. The guard therefore reads as 'the const matches the struct' while actually only checking the subset of fields that fixture happens to populate. A new field added with skip_serializing_if and omitted from the const would not be caught.

This is the .claude/rules/testing.md failure mode verbatim — same-shaped fixtures that cannot vary along the axis under test. The fix is multiple fixtures chosen so their union emits every serializable key, which is the approach selfie-6lz4's new test_known_dotfile_fields_matches_struct uses (a template entry plus a provider entry, because every DotfileEntry field but target is skip_serializing_if).

Found while planning selfie-6lz4.
acceptance_criteria: The guard fails when a serializable field is added to Package without being added to KNOWN_PACKAGE_FIELDS, including a field with skip_serializing_if.

title: A relative target skips while an escaping template aborts, and the docs say otherwise
description:
Two refusals in SecretApply are decided from the entry alone, before anything executes, and they return different outcomes:

- usable_target (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:631) — a non-absolute target returns SecretOutcome::Skipped
- refuse_unresolvable (:657) — a template escaping the package directory returns SecretOutcome::Failed

handle_apply (:1042) consults stop_on_error only for Failed. So an escaping template ends the run while a relative target never does, though neither ran a command.

docs/package-files.md describes the opposite for the first: 'A dry run does still apply every check that can be made without running anything — a target that is not absolute, a template escaping the package directory — … Because those refusals are failures, stop_on_error (default true) ends the preview at the first one rather than listing every remaining problem entry.'

Reproduce with two provider entries, the first with a relative target and the second absolute, stop_on_error at its default: the run warns about the first and continues, in a dry run and a real apply. Secondary effect: the refused entry lands in skipped_count next to 'already in sync'.

Decide which behavior is wanted and make code and docs agree. Treating both as failures matches the documentation and is the more defensible reading, since a refused entry is not a skipped one.
acceptance_criteria: Both entry-level refusals produce the same outcome, and the documentation matches it.

title: User-facing text not updated for what provider-sourced dotfiles changed
description:
PR #31 and PR #34 both established that when behavior changes, the CLI help and MCP tool descriptions describing it must change too; both were fixed at the time. Provider-sourced dotfiles updated four MCP descriptions and missed the rest.

- crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs:668 — selfie_dotfiles_drift still says 'Check deployed dotfiles for drift between repo sources and targets. Returns per-file drift status.' Secret-bearing entries are never checked (dotfile_service/service.rs:1316 skips them as 'provider-sourced (not verifiable without resolving)'), so an assistant reading only the description has no reason to treat 'no drift' as partial.
- crates/cli/src/cli.rs:556 — --dry-run still says 'Show what would change without writing', but a dry run deliberately does not resolve secret-bearing entries and so cannot say whether they would change.
- crates/cli/src/cli.rs:560 — --yes still says 'Auto-accept overwrite for conflicts (non-interactive mode)', but auto_accept is deliberately not consulted for secret-bearing entries.
- crates/cli/src/cli.rs:429 and :438 — the dotfiles drift and list subcommand help describe the old behavior, with no mention that a class of entries is skipped.
- crates/cli/src/commands/dotfiles/list.rs:49 — the column is still headed 'Source' while list.rs:60 renders 'command: op read op://…' or 'creds.tpl (vars: api_key)' into it. The MCP counterpart replaced the flat field with a kind discriminator for exactly this reason.
- docs/configuration.md:198 — command_timeout is still 'Default timeout for package operations in seconds'. It now also bounds every provider command and every template binding, per command; docs/package-files.md:572 states this and notes an entry with several bindings can take longer in total. The project's documentation rule names docs/configuration.md as the file to update for config settings.

Each is one line. Grouped because it is one pass over user-facing text, not six investigations.
acceptance_criteria: CLI help, MCP tool descriptions and docs/configuration.md describe what the code now does.

title: MCP apply and drift events overload one field with two kinds of value
description:
PR #40 raised this pattern on crates/mcp-server/src/event_collector.rs:88 — a field that is 'sometimes an enum-like value and sometimes a free-form reason string … makes the field inconsistent and harder for clients to parse reliably' — and it was fixed then. Provider-sourced dotfiles reintroduces it on adjacent fields.

crates/mcp-server/src/event_collector.rs:203 emits dotfile_conflict.diff, which for a repository file is a unified diff and for a secret-bearing entry is the human-readable summary from dotfile_service/service.rs:511 ('target exists and differs from resolved output / resolved output : 3 lines / (content hidden)'). Similarly dotfile_deployed.source (:187), dotfile_skipped.source (:192) and dotfile_conflict.source are a filesystem path for one kind of entry and secret_origin() output — 'command: op read op://…' — for the other.

The same change introduced a 'kind' discriminator for selfie_dotfiles_list precisely because a flat source field no longer described the data. That discriminator was not carried into the apply and drift events, so the two MCP surfaces now describe the same entry under different contracts. An assistant that learns the shape from one cannot rely on it in the other.
acceptance_criteria: An MCP client can tell from the payload which kind of value a field holds, consistently across list, apply and drift.

title: Revealing a conflict shows an unreadable target as empty
description:
secret_conflict_summary deliberately distinguishes a target that exists but cannot be read from one that is empty — its own comment says reporting '0 lines' 'would read as an empty file and understate what an overwrite destroys'. The reveal path then does exactly that.

crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:876 collapses the state before handing it to the resolver: current.unwrap_or_default().to_vec() turns Unreadable into b"". ConflictDetail::Secret (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/port.rs:44) carries current as a plain &[u8] with no way to express the difference.

So for a target that exists but cannot be read — chmod 000, or root-owned under a writable parent — apply prints 'current target: exists but could not be read', the user selects Reveal, and sees either a diff rendering every line as an addition against an apparently empty file, or 'current target : 0 bytes'. Both contradict the summary shown two lines earlier and understate what Accept destroys.

Fix by carrying the state through to the resolver, or by having reveal refuse when the target was unreadable.
acceptance_criteria: Revealing a conflict on an unreadable target says it could not be read rather than showing it as empty.

title: Docs reference a top-level 'selfie install' command that does not exist
description:
Two user-facing places tell the reader to run 'selfie install', which is not a command. The top-level subcommands are spec, package, apply, dotfiles, sync, track, config and completion (crates/cli/src/cli.rs); install lives under package, so the command is 'selfie package install'.

- crates/cli/src/main.rs:19 — the crate's module doc lists 'selfie install <package>  # Install a package'
- docs/getting-started.md:51 — 'After restarting your shell, selfie install <TAB> will show available package names'

The second is worse than a stale doc: it tells a new user to test their shell completion with a command that cannot complete, so completion appears broken when it is not.

Both predate provider-sourced dotfiles and were found while reviewing it. Note a stale worktree config in this repo carries a bd command about 'flattening CLI command structure (selfie install vs selfie package install)', so promoting the common verbs to the top level may have been considered — if that is still wanted, these docs become correct instead of needing a fix.
acceptance_criteria: Every documented command invocation matches what the CLI accepts.

title: Security audit of a selfie setup, exposed to both the CLI and MCP
description:
Report the security posture of what selfie manages on this machine: permissions on deployed targets, what executes on apply, and configuration that undermines the guarantees the dotfile design makes.

PLACEMENT. In the library, exposed through both adapters — not in selfie-mcp. CLAUDE.md puts logic in the library and presentation in adapters, and an MCP-only audit would be invisible to CLI users while putting real logic in an adapter. One implementation, a table for the CLI and structured JSON for an assistant.

NAMING. 'audit' is taken: selfie audit runs the user's own audit command to detect installation sources, and MCP exposes selfie_package_audit and selfie_package_audit_all. Pick something else; 'doctor' follows the cargo/brew/flutter convention.

CHECKS. Each of these is something found by hand while building provider-sourced dotfiles, which is the argument that they check real things:

- A managed target readable by group or other. Owner-only means mode & 0o077 == 0; a 0640 credential leaks to the group, which on a shared machine is exactly who it is being hidden from.
- The deploy state file's own mode (selfie-b5i4).
- A target that is a symlink, since deploys currently write through them (selfie-4m9).
- A vars command that contains a literal secret rather than fetching one — 'echo hunter2' puts the secret in the package file and in process listings. Already documented as an anti-pattern.
- Which packages execute commands on apply, and how many. The Info notice already computes this per package; the audit aggregates it so a package directory can be assessed as a whole.
- A target whose PARENT directory is world-writable. write_file_private protects the file and explicitly does not protect the directory, so this is the gap it leaves.
- Permissions on the package and dotfiles directories.

All of it is stat plus files selfie already parses. No new dependencies.

TWO HAZARDS TO DESIGN AGAINST, not to discover later.

A passing audit must not read as 'this setup is secure'. It checks a fixed list. State what was checked, and do not summarize as a pass/fail verdict that invites the reading that everything unchecked is fine.

The output is itself a map of where every credential on the machine lives. Handing that to an assistant is defensible — it is the user's own tool, and the deploy state file already holds the same paths — but it should be a stated trade in the tool description rather than a side effect nobody decided on.

The audit must never execute a provider command, for the same reason enumeration does not: it would reach a secret store and can raise an authentication prompt from a read-only operation.
acceptance_criteria: One library implementation reports the checks above; the CLI renders a table and MCP returns structured JSON; no provider command runs; the output does not present itself as a security verdict.
notes: Raised by the user reading ADR-0003 in PR #67 and asking whether security auditing could be available, possibly via MCP so an assistant could run it.

title: Revisit whether secret-bearing dotfiles can carry drift state under a keyed MAC
description:
ADR-0003 refuses to record anything derived from a secret, because an unsalted hash in the deploy state file is a confirmation oracle: anyone able to read that file can test candidate values offline. The cost is that selfie cannot distinguish a rotated secret from a hand-edited target, so both produce a conflict prompt on every apply — the friction a daily driver feels most.

A user-supplied salt does NOT lift the objection. The salt has to be stored beside the hash to recompute it, so the same reader gets both and can still verify guesses. Salt defeats precomputation and reuse across targets, not verification. For a high-entropy token the oracle was already academic; for a low-entropy secret, salt does not help.

A keyed MAC does lift it, if the key is somewhere the state-file reader cannot reach. Selfie already has a mechanism for fetching a secret without storing it — the provider command — so the key could be an ordinary binding such as 'op read op://Private/selfie-state-key'. That reuses the existing design instead of building key storage, which is what ADR-0001 and ADR-0003 both insist on.

Decide this properly rather than adding a config knob. It changes ADR-0003's central invariant from one that is checkable by grep — nothing secret-derived is persisted — to one requiring reasoning about key custody, key rotation, and the failure mode when the key cannot be fetched because the machine is offline or the user is not signed in. Falling back to no-state-and-prompt is the obvious answer but should be stated.

Note the cheaper alternative first: the oracle argument depends on the state file being easier to read than the secret. It is currently 0644 while secret targets are 0600 (selfie-b5i4). Fix that and the asymmetry largely evaporates, at which point a plain checksum may suffice and none of this key management is needed. Evaluate that before the MAC.
acceptance_criteria: An ADR amendment records whether secret-bearing entries may carry drift state, and under what protection.
notes: Raised by the user reading ADR-0003 in PR #67, asking whether a user-configured salt would open up the functionality the ADR gave up.

title: Trait docs describe adapter behavior that other implementors do not share
description:
Several port method docs describe how RealFileSystem or ShellCommandRunner implements them rather than what the port guarantees. In a codebase built on ports and adapters that is a contract error, not a style preference: a second implementor inherits documentation that is false for it, and callers may rely on behavior only one adapter provides.

The sharpest case is FileSystem::write_file_private (crates/selfie/src/fs/filesystem.rs). Its doc explains that the symlink guarantee 'survives exactly when expand_path on the full path fails', reasoning about canonicalization — but canonicalizing is RealFileSystem::expand_path's behavior, and the trait's expand_path contract never promises it. So the port documents a cross-method interaction that exists in exactly one adapter, and the stated rule is false for MockFileSystem or any future one. The same doc also describes the temporary-file mechanism, the tempfile backend's per-platform behavior, and MoveFileEx semantics.

FileSystem::is_owner_only has it too: 'on every other platform this returns true' is what RealFileSystem does, not something every implementor must honor.

The split to apply. Trait: what a caller may rely on and an implementor must provide — owner-only and atomic replacement, no world-readable window, a symlink at the final component replaced while parents are followed, that the guarantee applies to the path as given so a resolving caller can forfeit it, and that an implementation which cannot determine owner-only returns true meaning 'nothing to tighten'. Impl: the temp-file-then-rename mechanism, the tempfile backend, per-platform specifics, mode & 0o077 on Unix, and the precise expand_path canonicalization rule.

Affects roughly six methods added or changed by the provider-sourced dotfiles work: write_file_private, is_owner_only, read_file_bytes, execute_in_dir, read_referenced_file, and ConflictResolver::resolve.

Doc-only and zero behavior risk, but not mechanical: each moved claim must be re-verified against the implementation rather than copy-pasted. Three doc claims in this area were found false during that work — the non-Unix platform guarantee, ~user expansion, and what borrowing prevents a resolver from doing — so a bulk move is exactly where a fourth would enter.
acceptance_criteria: Port docs state contracts only; adapter-specific behavior lives on the impl; every moved claim is verified against the code it now describes.
notes: Raised by the user reviewing PR #67. Deliberately not fixed there: it would have been the sixth commit after the branch's independent review approval.

title: Decide what invariant a dotfile target path should satisfy
description:
A dotfile target must be absolute or start with ~/, enforced in three places (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs, in handle_apply, check_drift and the secret-bearing path) and documented in docs/package-files.md.

The stated rationale is that a relative target would resolve against the process working directory, so selfie apply would deploy to different places depending on where it was run. That reasoning is right, but it is not the only rule that achieves it: resolving bare-relative targets against $HOME would equally eliminate CWD dependence, and is what yadm, chezmoi and stow effectively do. Nearly every target is under $HOME, so requiring ~/ on each entry is ceremony that buys nothing over a home-relative default.

The argument for keeping it is that selfie is not only a dotfile manager — it deploys to system paths too, and under home-relative defaults 'etc/nginx.conf' and '/etc/nginx.conf' differ by one character and mean very different things. Absolute-required makes that mistake unrepresentable.

The gap worth deciding on is neither of those. The rule enforces determinism within one machine and says nothing about portability across machines, which is selfie's whole premise. Both permitted forms are not equal: '~/.gemrc' works everywhere, '/Users/sloveless/.gemrc' works on one machine. And selfie's own tooling produces the non-portable one — see selfie-h15, where track_dotfile records the expanded absolute path. So the tool violates by default the convention the rule leaves to the user.

Decide which invariant targets should satisfy: not-CWD-relative as now, or portable-across-machines, which would mean preferring or requiring ~/ for anything under $HOME and treating a bare absolute path as a deliberate escape hatch for system paths.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded, in an ADR if it changes the rule, and the enforcement and documentation match it.
notes:
Sharper statement of the problem, from comparing the target rule with the source rule.

Both rules serve one principle: a package file must not contain paths that depend on incidental location. Source enforces it completely — relative-only, no absolute, no '..', so the path cannot escape the package directory and cannot depend on where the repository happens to be cloned. Target enforces it only halfway: '~/.gemrc' honors the principle, while '/Users/sloveless/.gemrc' is exactly a path that depends on incidental location, and both are permitted.

So the inconsistency is not between the source and target rules, which are coherent opposites. It is inside the target rule, which admits one form that satisfies the principle and one that defeats it — and per selfie-h15, selfie's own tooling emits the form that defeats it.

title: Provider stderr can carry secret material into events
description:
A failing dotfile provider command has its stderr forwarded, truncated, into the error path so that stop_on_error is actionable — without some diagnostic a failed credential deploy is undebuggable. stderr is content selfie does not control: a provider invoked with a verbose or debug flag can echo secret material there, and it would reach an error event and the MCP server's JSON.

Mitigated rather than solved: stderr is forwarded on failure only, never on the success path, and it is length-bounded. Documented in docs/package-files.md as a known sharp edge.

A real fix needs a way to give the user a diagnostic without relaying untrusted output verbatim — an exit code plus a fixed message, an opt-in flag to include stderr, or redaction. Related to selfie-ppp, which is the same exposure for command stdout on every command path.
acceptance_criteria: A failed provider gives an actionable diagnostic without relaying its stderr verbatim by default.

title: A dotfile that failed to deploy still yields a success exit code
description:
With stop_on_error false, a resolve or write failure is counted as skipped and the run still returns OperationSuccess::DotfilesApplied, so selfie apply exits 0 having failed to deploy a file.

Pre-existing behavior for repository-file failures, but it matters more now that a failure can be a credential that did not deploy: a script or CI step checking the exit code is told everything worked.
acceptance_criteria: A run in which any dotfile failed to deploy reports failure, or the distinction is explicit in the exit code contract.
notes:
FOURTH ROUTE, from selfie-n310's unit: an entry refused because its var name cannot be substituted, or because a _-prefixed anchor collides with a real field, is emitted as PackageEvent::Warning and counted in skipped_count. crates/cli/src/event_processor.rs:167-169 sets exit_code = 1 only for PackageEvent::Error, so 'selfie apply' still exits 0 having refused to deploy.

Not made worse by that unit — it is the same accounting every other refusal already used, and the refusals themselves are the point of the fix. Recorded so the count of ways to exit 0 without deploying stays accurate: repository-file failures, secret resolve failures, symlinked targets (selfie-4m9), and now invalid entries.

title: Path containment guard is lexical and does not follow symlinks
description:
crates/selfie/src/paths.rs is_within compares paths lexically, deliberately, because it must work on paths that do not yet exist. A symlink inside the package directory therefore passes the check while pointing outside it: packages/creds/link.tpl -> ../outside.tpl is accepted and the outside file's contents are rendered into a deployed dotfile.

Applies to all three callers: the repository-file apply path, PackageRepository::read_referenced_file, and the template read path.

Low severity — it needs a hostile package repository, and such a repository can already run arbitrary commands through a dotfile's command field, so this guard is not the security boundary in that scenario. Filed because the guard's doc comment claims to prevent exactly this.

Fix means widening the check: symlink_metadata per component, or canonicalizing the parent where it exists.
acceptance_criteria: Either the guard rejects symlinked escapes, or its documentation states it is lexical only.

title: Template scanner is quadratic on unmatched opening braces
description:
crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/template.rs: scan re-searches the whole remaining template for a closing }} at every {{ it encounters. A large template containing many opening braces and no closing pair makes the search walk the rest of the buffer once per opening brace.

Reachable from validation, not only apply: validate_all reads and scans every template, so selfie spec validate --all can hang on one pathological file rather than merely slowing down. Templates are user-authored, which lowers severity, but a hang is a different failure from a slowdown.

Documented as accepted in the code. Bounding it means restructuring the scanner, which was out of scope for a review fix.
acceptance_criteria: A template with many unmatched opening braces cannot make validation hang.

title: stop_on_error does not stop on most dotfile errors
description:
SelfieConfig::stop_on_error defaults to true, but in the dotfile apply path it governs only secret-bearing resolution failures. Repository-file failures in the same loop — unreadable source, write failure, path-traversal rejection — have always continued past the error and still do.

Provider-sourced dotfiles implemented the flag for its own failures because the spec required it, and deliberately did not retrofit it onto the pre-existing paths, since that would change existing behavior beyond that feature's scope. The boundary is documented in code.

The result is a setting whose name promises more than it delivers: a user setting stop_on_error=true reasonably expects an apply to halt on any error, and it does not.
acceptance_criteria: stop_on_error either governs all dotfile apply failures, or its documented scope matches its name.

title: Dotfile validation errors carry field paths, not line numbers
description:
The provider-sourced dotfiles spec requires content-source errors to be 'reported against the offending line via Spanned<T>'. They are not: DotfileEntry's fields are plain String rather than Spanned, so dotfile diagnostics identify the offending entry by field path (dotfiles[0].command) rather than by line and column.

This is a known deviation shipped with the feature and documented as such, not a design choice. The rest of the package model migrated to Spanned<T> precisely so validation could point at the offending line; dotfiles are the remaining exception.

Fix means making DotfileEntry's fields Spanned and threading the spans through the dotfile validation path.
acceptance_criteria: Dotfile content-source validation errors report a line and column like other package validation errors.

title: Command output capture is unbounded before any size limit applies
description:
Secret-bearing dotfile resolution caps resolved content at MAX_CONTENT_BYTES, but the cap is post-hoc: execute_with_timeout has already buffered the command's entire output into a Vec before the check runs. The cap bounds what gets written and compared, not what gets allocated.

Not a new exposure — every install, check and audit command already buffers unbounded output — but the dotfiles documentation should not imply the cap is a memory bound, and it isn't one.

Fix would be streaming-bounded capture in CommandRunner, aborting once a limit is exceeded, which benefits every command path rather than just dotfiles.
acceptance_criteria: A command producing unbounded output cannot exhaust memory, or the limitation is documented accurately wherever a cap is advertised.

title: selfie info should report that apply executes commands
description:
Dotfile entries with vars or a command cause 'selfie apply' to execute user-defined commands, which changes apply from a pure file-copy operation into an executing one. That is surfaced in selfie validate, but the spec also asks for it in selfie info, and package/service/info.rs currently emits no dotfile information at all.

Requires a new PackageInfoData field plus CLI and MCP rendering. Matters most for shared or overlaid package directories, where a reader may treat a package file as data.
acceptance_criteria: selfie info reports a package's dotfile content sources and how many commands apply would execute.

title: Warn when a dotfile var binding's binary is not on PATH
description:
The provider-sourced dotfiles spec asks validation to warn per binding when the command's binary is absent from PATH, using is_command_available, so a package can report that op is present but teller is missing.

Not implemented with the feature: is_command_available is an async CommandRunner call, while Package::validate() is synchronous and has no runner. Wiring a CommandRunner into the validation path is a larger change than the feature it would serve, so it was deliberately deferred rather than bolted on.

Note this check is necessarily advisory — PATH at validate time is not PATH at apply time, particularly for the MCP server, which uses a login shell precisely because GUI-launched processes do not inherit terminal PATH.
acceptance_criteria: Validation reports missing provider binaries per binding without making Package::validate() async or filesystem-dependent.

title: Deploy state can outlive a lost rename after a crash
description:
perform_deploy (crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:478-491) records deploy state immediately after writing. With an atomic rename but no directory fsync, a power loss can lose the rename while the state record survives, so drift detection would report a file clean that has actually reverted to its previous content.

Skipping the directory fsync is a defensible trade in the write path itself (losing the rename just means the deploy did not happen, and re-running apply fixes it). The gap is that the state layer records success before that durability is established. Fix belongs in the state layer, not the filesystem adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Deploy state cannot claim a deployment that a crash discarded, or the limitation is documented as accepted.

title: test_permission_denied cannot fail and shells out to chmod
description:
crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:250-288. The only assertion is 'if let Err(FileSystemError::IoError(_)) = result { }' — an empty body, so the test passes whatever read_file returns. It also shells out to chmod via std::process::Command and discards the result, which conflicts with CLAUDE.md's rule that tests must not alter the development environment.

Either make it assert a real outcome, or delete it. A test that cannot fail is worse than no test because it reads as coverage.
acceptance_criteria: The test asserts a real outcome or is removed; no shelling out to chmod.

title: pretty_assertions is a runtime dependency of the selfie library
description: crates/selfie/Cargo.toml:14 declares pretty_assertions = "1.4.1" under [dependencies] rather than [dev-dependencies], so a test-assertion crate is compiled into the library build and ships to consumers. Move it to [dev-dependencies] and confirm nothing in non-test code refers to it.
acceptance_criteria: pretty_assertions is a dev-dependency; cargo build succeeds; cargo test still passes.

title: Prompt-for-input dotfile vars for stores without a CLI
description:
Dotfile template vars bind a name to a command. That requires the secret store to have a CLI. Users of GUI-only or web-only password managers cannot participate.

Add a var binding kind that makes selfie prompt for the value on stdin instead of executing a command, so the user can copy from their manager and paste. Value is used for that apply only and never persisted, consistent with secret-bearing dotfiles holding no deploy state.

Design sketch: this needs a new port alongside ConflictResolver in dotfile_service/port.rs, since the library must not read stdin directly. The CLI adapter implements it with dialoguer's Password prompt so input is not echoed; the MCP server and any non-interactive caller implement it as an error rather than blocking forever on a read that will never return.

Consequences to weigh before building: every apply touching such an entry becomes interactive, which conflicts with unattended use; and with no caching the user re-pastes on every apply, which may push people toward pasting secrets into shell history instead.
acceptance_criteria: A var binding can request interactive input; the value is never persisted or logged; non-interactive callers fail with a clear error rather than hanging.
notes: Raised during selfie-doh design. Deliberately deferred to keep that feature shippable; the port-based approach means it can be added without changing the entry model.

title: Evaluate whether YAML is the right format for package files
description:
Package files are YAML, parsed via serde-saphyr with Spanned<T> for error locations. Worth evaluating whether another format serves better before the format calcifies with more users.

Arguments for staying: serde-saphyr + Spanned<T> was a deliberate investment for good validation errors; YAML is familiar and widely known; templates live in separate files so YAML's awkward multi-line string modes are not hit; nothing in the dotfile templating design pressures the format.

Arguments against: YAML's implicit type coercion surprises (the Norway problem); significant whitespace; comments are lost on programmatic rewrite, which matters because selfie edits package files via spec create/update and the MCP server; no schema enforcement without extra tooling.

Alternatives worth weighing: TOML (simpler, no significant whitespace, comment-preserving via toml_edit, weaker for deep nesting); KDL (good ergonomics, small ecosystem); Starlark/Dhall/Nickel (only justified if package files ever need logic, which is contrary to the declarative plus shell-out philosophy).

Cost of switching is broad rather than deep: every command, the MCP server, validation, span reporting, docs, and all existing package files. No backward compatibility is required pre-release.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded as an ADR, either affirming YAML with reasons or selecting a replacement with a migration outline.
notes: Raised while designing selfie-doh, when templating prompted the question of format fit. Deliberately kept separate: nothing in the dotfile templating design depends on the answer, and deciding it as a side effect of a feature would be the wrong way to settle it.

title: dotfiles list/track/remove should reflect per-environment dotfiles
description: The per-environment dotfiles core (34558ef) wired apply + drift to the effective set, but 'dotfiles list' (CLI list.rs, MCP server.rs) and the track/remove readers still use package.dotfiles() (shared only), so environment-specific dotfiles do not appear in listings and are not considered by remove's cleanup/track's display. Decide list semantics (effective set for current env, or list all with an environment label) and update accordingly. Follow-up to per-environment dotfiles core.
close_reason: list (CLI+MCP), track, and remove now use Package::dotfiles_with_scope() to reflect environment-specific dotfiles; CLI Environment column + MCP environment field; TDD.

title: Richer dotfile conflict resolution (backup-then-overwrite, merge) beyond accept/skip
description: On an apply conflict (existing target differs from selfie's source and may be user-authored), selfie currently offers accept (overwrite) or skip, and shows a unified diff. Enhancement: offer safer/richer resolution options, e.g. back up the existing target (.bak) before overwriting, open a merge tool / 3-way merge, or apply per-hunk. The core safety guarantee (never overwrite divergent content without consent) already holds and is recorded in ADR-0001 (Overwrite safety); this is about better ergonomics when a conflict does occur. The diff is already produced; merging is the hard part. Raised 2026-07-23 during ADR-0001 review.

title: selfie requires a config file to exist even when all settings are passed via CLI flags
description: During fresh-machine recovery proof (2026-07-23): running 'selfie apply' with HOME pointed at a clean dir failed with 'No configuration file found in locations: <HOME>/.config/selfie' even though --package-directory, --environment, and --state-directory were all supplied on the CLI. selfie should be able to run fully from CLI flags (and/or env vars) with no config file present — important for fresh-machine bootstrap, scripted/bulk operations, CI, containers, and ephemeral AI-driven runs. Workaround today: create ~/.config/selfie/config.yml first. Consider: treat missing config file as empty-config when required values come from flags, or add a way to point at an explicit config path.

title: CLI: add non-interactive way to attach a dotfile to an existing package (parity with MCP selfie_dotfiles_add)
description: 'selfie track <file>' is fully interactive (prompts existing-package vs standalone) with no flags to bypass it, so it can't be scripted or used in automation/bulk migration. The MCP server already has a non-interactive 'selfie_dotfiles_add' (add file to an existing package's dotfiles section). Add a CLI equivalent, e.g. 'selfie dotfiles add <file> --package <name>' or non-interactive flags on 'track'. Surfaced 2026-07-23 while migrating bat off YADM. Lower priority since the AI/MCP path is the primary driver, but needed for scriptable bulk migration of ~170 dotfiles.

title: Audit selfie for other silent-failure paths; make them warn or error
description: Follow-up to the config-unknown-keys bug. Sweep the codebase for places where selfie swallows errors or degrades silently (e.g. best-effort steps that skip without notice, ignored parse results, dropped fields). Each should surface a warning/error via PackageEvent so the user is never surprised. Establishes 'no silent failures' as a selfie design value. Reference: strategic-direction memory + docs runbook 2026-07-23.

title: Implement environment name completer
description: Create a custom completer for the --environment/-e global flag that suggests known environment names. These can be extracted by scanning package files for their environment keys. This is lower priority than package name completion but still useful — users often forget exact environment labels.

title: Consider suppressing redundant success message on completion
description: After commands like `selfie package status`, the default Completed event handler prints a line like `✓ Package 'foo' status checked successfully (2/2 steps)`. This is redundant when the command already displayed its results (e.g., the status table). Consider suppressing or shortening this message for commands where the output itself implies success.
close_reason: Suppressed redundant success messages in status, info, audit, and check commands

title: Expand SelfieConfig validation
description: Current config validation only checks environment (non-empty) and package_directory (non-empty, absolute). Add validation for dotfiles_directory and state_directory (absolute path when set), and validate that command_timeout is reasonable (warn if >600s). Also consider validating that package_directory and dotfiles_directory exist on disk (as warnings, not errors).
close_reason: Closed

title: Remove custom validation code after garde adoption
description: Once garde handles validation via derive macros, remove: validate.rs hand-written validators, ValidationIssue/ValidationIssues types (replaced by garde's error types), the extra_fields serde(flatten) hack for unknown field detection (serde-saphyr + garde handles this natively). This is cleanup after the garde migration.
close_reason: Superseded — garde not being adopted, so there's no custom validation code to remove after adoption.

title: Improve CI workflow
description:
The CI workflow needs several improvements:
1. (DONE) Double-run fixed — push: now filtered to main only.
2. Add clippy job — it's in the pre-commit checklist but not in CI.
3. The format job auto-commits and pushes on failure, which triggers another CI run. Should just fail instead (let developers fix locally).
4. Consider adding cargo cache for faster builds.
5. Consider adding a Rust toolchain cache.
close_reason: Fixed in c31bf34. Added clippy, rust-cache, removed auto-push, cleaned up job names and deps.

title: Surface drift-check failures in sync status
description: collect_drift_summary() ignores OperationResult::Failure from the drift stream, causing sync status to report empty/zero drift values and overall success when drift checking actually failed. Should surface the failure as a warning event. Copilot PR #35 comment 2978720110.
close_reason: Fixed: collect_drift_summary now captures OperationResult::Failure and emits a warning event

title: Convert fast_forward to native gix ref update + checkout
description: fast_forward currently shells out to git merge --ff-only. Convert to native gix: verify ancestor relationship, update ref, then checkout working tree via gix-worktree-state. Requires adding worktree-state feature to gix dependency. User accepts larger binary for consistency.

title: Convert push/fetch to native gix transport
description: push and fetch currently shell out to git CLI for SSH/credential integration. Convert to gix's blocking-network-client transport. Requires adding the blocking-network-client feature to gix dependency. User accepts larger binary for consistency. May need to handle SSH agent integration via gix-transport.
notes: Assessment (2026-03-24, gix 0.81.0): Push is still incomplete in gix 0.81.0 — thin pack creation works but actual push protocol is not implemented. Fetch works with blocking-network-client feature but adds binary size and complexity for marginal benefit over reliable git CLI shell-out. Recommend revisiting when gix push matures (track gitoxide releases). The gix upgrade from 0.72→0.81 was done separately.

title: Convert remaining run_git calls to native gix
description: stage_files and commit are now pure gix. Remaining run_git calls for local ops that should be converted: discover_repo (branch via rev-parse, remote name), repo_status (ls-files --deleted), diff_commits (diff --name-status), ahead_behind_counts (rev-list). Network ops (push, fetch) and fast_forward (merge --ff-only) are fine as shell-outs.

title: Update docs for sync commands
description: Update README.md status section, docs/configuration.md with sync commands. Add docs/sync.md with usage examples for status/push/pull, flag reference, conventional commit format explanation, and MCP tool descriptions.
close_reason: Added docs/sync.md with complete sync guide. Updated README.md status section and navigation. dprint formatted.

title: Add requires_sudo flag per environment in package specs
description: Allow package specs to declare requires_sudo: true per environment, so selfie can warn or prompt before running commands that need elevated privileges. Nice UX touch for packages that need sudo on some environments but not others. Found in selfie2 old repo.

title: Support multiple package directories in config
description: Allow configuring multiple package_directory paths (e.g., a personal directory and a shared team directory). Packages from all directories would be discovered and available. Current config only supports a single package_directory. Found in selfie-v1, selfie2, and investigation-selfie old repos.

title: Auto-detect installation source from executable path
description: Enhance the audit system with a fallback heuristic that detects how a package was installed by examining its executable path. For example: /opt/homebrew/bin/ → brew, ~/.cargo/bin/ → cargo, /usr/local/bin/ → manual/unknown. This would provide audit info even when no explicit audit command is defined in the package spec. Found in narcissist and investigation-selfie old repos.

title: Add search command to find packages by keyword
description: Add a 'search' or 'spec search' command that searches package files by name, description, tags, or other metadata. Useful once the user has many packages defined. Found in selfie2 spec (was planned but not implemented).
close_reason: Implemented spec search command with case-insensitive substring matching on name and description

title: Add per-environment configs to package specs
description: Currently configs is a top-level field that applies across all environments. Add support for per-environment config entries so users can deploy different config files per environment (e.g. ~/.gitconfig-personal on personal machines, ~/.gitconfig-work on work machines). Design should follow whatever pattern the environment inheritance feature establishes, rather than inventing a separate filtering mechanism. Blocked by environment inheritance design.

title: Remove version field from package YAML schema
description: The version field in package definitions is vestigial — selfie never compares versions, there's no upgrade logic, and git tracks definition history better than a hand-bumped semver. Remove it entirely: drop from Package struct, remove from validation, stop emitting in spec create, update parser to ignore if present (don't break existing files). If we later need schema versioning (post-release), add a schema_version or selfie_min_version field at that point.
close_reason: Shipped in PR #32

title: Investigate flattening CLI command structure
description: Evaluate moving runtime package commands to top-level: 'selfie install X' instead of 'selfie package install X'. Now that groups are off the table (replaced by recommends), the 'package' namespace adds typing without value for the hot-path commands (install, check, audit). Questions to answer: (1) What happens to 'selfie list' ambiguity (specs vs packages)? (2) Should 'selfie package list' and 'selfie spec list' stay namespaced? (3) Keep 'selfie package X' as aliases during transition or break cleanly? (4) How does this affect MCP server tool naming? (5) Does 'selfie apply' already set the precedent for top-level verbs?

title: Investigate flattening CLI command structure (selfie install vs selfie package install)
description:
Now that 'selfie group' commands are off the table (replaced by recommends), the 'selfie package' namespace may be unnecessary overhead for the most common commands. Investigate promoting runtime verbs to top-level:

- selfie install ripgrep (instead of selfie package install ripgrep)
- selfie check ripgrep
- selfie audit ripgrep
- selfie apply ripgrep (already top-level)

Open questions to resolve:
- What happens to 'selfie list'? Ambiguous between spec list and package list. Maybe defaults to package list with status?
- Should 'selfie package install' remain as an alias for backward compat, or break it (pre-1.0)?
- Does the spec subcommand stay as-is? (Probably yes — definition management is less frequent)
- How does this affect the MCP server tool naming?
- Impact on shell completions and help text organization
- Does 'selfie status' make sense as top-level too?

This is an investigation ticket — answer the questions, then decide whether to proceed.
close_reason: Duplicate of selfie-gyb

title: Rename package config deployment to 'dotfile' terminology
description:
The word 'config' is overloaded in the codebase: SelfieConfig (selfie's settings), ConfigEntry/ConfigService (package file deployment), and the 'selfie config' CLI subcommand. Rename the package config deployment layer to use 'dotfile' instead.

Scope of changes:
- YAML schema: configs: → dotfiles:, configs_directory → dotfiles_directory in selfie config
- Types: ConfigEntry → DotfileEntry, ConfigService → DotfileService, ConfigServiceImpl → DotfileServiceImpl
- Module: config_service/ → dotfile_service/ (or dotfile/)
- Events: ConfigDeploying → DotfileDeploying, ConfigDeployed → DotfileDeployed, etc.
- CLI: apply command internals (the 'selfie apply' command name stays the same)
- MCP server: tool names and descriptions that reference 'config' in the deployment sense
- Docs: package-files.md, configuration.md, README examples
- Tests: all config_service_tests

This is a pure rename refactor with no behavior changes. Should be done as a focused PR separate from feature work.
close_reason: Duplicate of selfie-ybf

title: Track and display last check/install timestamps
description:
Persist timestamps for when each package was last checked or installed, and display this in info/list output. Helps users identify stale packages that haven't been verified in a while.

This is a larger feature because selfie currently has no persistent state beyond the package YAML files and config. It requires a new storage mechanism for run history.

Implementation considerations:
- Need a state/history store — likely a simple JSON or SQLite file in the selfie config directory (~/.config/selfie/state.db or similar).
- Following hexagonal architecture, the state store should be behind a trait/port (e.g., RunHistoryProvider).
- Record: package name, operation type (check/install/audit), timestamp, result (success/failure).
- Display in info command: 'Last checked: 3 days ago', 'Last installed: 2 weeks ago'.
- Display in list command: optional column or indicator for staleness.
