- Consider a --stale flag for list to filter packages not checked within N days.
- The MCP server should also be able to query this data.

title: Detect package manager availability before install
description:
Before running install/check/audit commands, detect whether the package manager binary (e.g., brew, npm, apt) referenced in the command actually exists on the system. Surface this as an early warning in info and list output rather than waiting for a cryptic command-not-found error at install time.

The codebase already has an is_command_available function using the which crate. This feature would parse the first token of install/check/audit commands to identify the binary, then check availability.

Implementation considerations:
- Parse the first token of each command string to extract the binary name. Handle pipes (use the first command), shell wrappers, etc.
- For list command, could show a warning indicator next to packages whose commands reference unavailable binaries.
- For info command, show per-environment binary availability.
- Emit via PackageEvent for frontend-agnostic rendering.
- Performance: which lookups are fast, but cache results since many packages may use the same binary (e.g., dozens of brew packages).

title: Install progress step count is wrong when dependencies are already installed
description: When running 'selfie package install', the total step count is calculated assuming every dependency needs full installation (fetch + env check + check + install command + verify). But dependencies that are already installed skip the install/verify steps, so the final count ends up lower than the total (e.g., '21/29 steps' when the operation is complete). The ProgressTracker total should be adjusted as dependencies are skipped, or the calculation should account for already-installed deps.
close_reason: ProgressTracker::reduce_total_steps(4) called when package already installed, correcting inflated step count

title: config validate checks post-override config, not on-disk file
description: The 'config validate' command validates config.selfie_config() after CLI overrides have been applied. This can mask problems in the on-disk config file (e.g., an invalid package_directory that becomes valid only due to a CLI flag override). Consider loading the raw file config inside this handler and validating that instead of the already-overridden CliConfig.
close_reason: handle_validate re-loads raw config from disk via YamlLoader instead of validating post-override config

title: handle_install returns was_already_installed=false for root package
description: handle_install in service/install.rs always returns OperationSuccess::package_installed(..., was_already_installed = false, executable_path = None) for the root package, even if the root was already installed. This loses information and can cause the CLI to report the wrong final status for no-op installs. Should track the root package's actual install result and use that when returning the final OperationResult.
close_reason: handle_install now returns the actual root package result instead of hardcoded was_already_installed=false

title: Fix verbose mode parity for check command
description: P3: install.rs forwards Progress events to default handler when verbose (returns false), but check.rs always suppresses Progress events (returns true) even in verbose mode. Users who set --verbose expect more output. check should forward Progress events to the default handler when verbose, matching install behavior.
close_reason: Implemented in commit a8ac5ff on feat/cli-display-consistency branch

title: Standardize indentation levels across output
description: P3: Three different indentation levels carry overlapping meanings. print_progress uses 2 spaces, print_field uses 2 spaces, check/validate format_key_fn uses 3 spaces, OperationHandle::add_output_line uses 2 spaces + │. Same visual concept (nested content / key-value pairs) uses different alignment. Pick one indentation for nested content and standardize.
close_reason: INDENT constant standardizes key-value indentation

title: Fix symbol semantic mismatches
description: P3: Two places use symbols with wrong semantics. 1) remove.rs:43 — print_info('✓ Package is not a dependency...') embeds success ✓ inside blue info message; should use print_success. 2) check.rs:106 — '⚠️ Check failed' uses warning symbol for a failure; symbol system says ✗ = failure, ⚠ = warning.
close_reason: Fixed print_info→print_success in remove.rs:48

title: Route static output through MultiProgress when spinners active
description: Phase 2 of indicatif display layer: DisplayManager's static output methods (print_info, print_error, etc.) currently use raw println\!/eprintln\! which will interleave with active spinners. When spinners are wired into more commands, these need to route through self.mp.println()/self.mp.suspend() to avoid visual corruption. Also remove #[allow(dead_code)] from the mp field and EventProcessor::display() accessor when used.
close_reason: Static output routed through MultiProgress

title: Wire ErrorCollector into event processing
description: Phase 2 of indicatif display layer: use DisplayManager::collect_error() and ErrorDetail to accumulate structured errors during multi-package operations, then print a copy-pasteable error summary at the end via DisplayManager::finish(). Currently ErrorDetail, ErrorCollector, collect_error(), and has_errors() exist but are unused (#[allow(dead_code)]). Remove the annotations when wired up. The EventProcessor already calls display.finish() after processing.
close_reason: JoinError metadata fix and ErrorCollector wiring implemented

title: Wire spinners into install/check/validate commands
description: Phase 2 of indicatif display layer: use DisplayManager::start_operation() and OperationHandle for animated spinners in install, check, and validate commands. Currently these commands use static print_progress() calls. The spinner infrastructure (start_operation, finish_success/failure/warning, OperationHandle) exists but is only used by the list command. Remove #[allow(dead_code)] from start_operation(), OperationHandle struct/impl, and the non-in-place finish methods when wired up.
close_reason: Duplicate of selfie-v5a, resolved in same commit

title: Graceful shutdown with tokio::signal — use existing PackageEvent::Canceled
description:
Implement Ctrl+C (SIGINT) handling using tokio::signal::ctrl_c() (already have tokio as a dependency — no new crate needed).

Current state: No signal handling exists. Ctrl+C during install orphans subprocesses. process::exit() is called in main.rs without cleanup. The PackageEvent::Canceled event type already exists in the event system but is never emitted by service code. The event processor already handles it (sets exit_code=1, prints warning).

Key changes needed:
- main.rs: Wrap dispatch_command in tokio::select! with ctrl_c() signal
- service.rs: Accept a CancellationToken (from tokio_util) or similar mechanism to propagate cancellation to spawned tasks
- shell.rs: On cancellation, kill running subprocess via child.kill().await and emit Canceled event

Note: spawned tasks currently use tokio::spawn() without retaining JoinHandle — this pattern needs adjustment for clean shutdown.

Depends on: Nothing, but this is the largest of the 5 items.
close_reason: Implemented graceful Ctrl+C shutdown with CancellationToken threaded through service and command runner layers

title: Add strum crate — derive Display/FromStr for enums
description:
Replace 10 hand-written impl Display for ... blocks with #[derive(strum::Display)].

Targets:
- event/metadata.rs: OperationType (7 match arms)
- event.rs: StepCount, OperationFailure, CommandFailure, DependencyFailure, OperationSuccess, CheckResult, ValidationStatus
- commands/runner.rs: OutputChunk
- validation.rs: ValidationErrorCategory (6 match arms)

Note: Some Display impls have complex formatting (e.g., CommandFailure includes exit code). strum supports #[strum(to_string = "...")] for simple cases but complex multi-field formatting should stay hand-written. Assess each impl individually.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add semver crate — replace hand-rolled version regex (may drop regex)
description:
Replace regex::Regex::new(r"^\d+\.\d+\.\d+") in package/validate.rs:164-167 with semver::Version::parse().

Behavior change: Current regex is permissive — 1.2.3xyz passes, pre-release like 1.2.3-beta passes. semver::Version::parse() is stricter (proper semver spec). This is the correct behavior for a version validation warning. Note the validation produces a warning, not an error, so stricter is fine.

Bonus: regex is used nowhere else in the codebase. Adopting semver lets us drop regex entirely (heavy transitive deps: regex-automata, regex-syntax, aho-corasick).

Maintained by dtolnay. Used by Cargo itself.
close_reason: Replaced regex with semver crate for version validation

title: Make selfie crate re-exports consistent
description: Several public types in the selfie crate are not re-exported from their parent modules, forcing consumers to use deep paths like selfie::fs::filesystem::FileSystemError instead of selfie::fs::FileSystemError. Audit all pub mod/pub use in the selfie crate and add re-exports so that commonly-used types are accessible from the module they logically belong to (e.g., fs::FileSystemError, package::event::error::StreamedError). This improves ergonomics for CLI and future consumer crates.
close_reason: Added pub use re-exports in event.rs, config.rs, fs.rs, and package.rs. Updated all CLI imports and doc examples to use shorter paths. Code reviewed and all issues fixed.

title: Fix 3 failing package_list_tests integration tests
description:
Three integration tests in crates/cli/tests/package_list_tests.rs are failing due to assertion mismatches on display formatting:

1. test_package_list_all_flag_not_relevant_status - expects 'No check' but gets 'N/A'
2. test_package_list_default_behavior_filters_by_environment - expects 'No check' but gets 'N/A'
3. test_package_list_environment_mismatch_shows_stats - expects 'No packages found for environment' but output format differs

These are pre-existing failures unrelated to the EventStream unification work.
close_reason: Fixed both bugs: status None vs NoCheckCommand, and environment_stats computed before filtering

title: Dual file-discovery code paths in YamlPackageRepository
description: YamlPackageRepository has two separate code paths for finding .yml/.yaml files: find_package_files (on the trait) uses path_exists twice, while find_package_files_with_context (internal, used by get_package) uses list_directory. The logic for resolving .yml vs .yaml extensions exists twice and should be unified — one should call the other.
close_reason: Unified in commit 1fb4df4: extracted filter_matching_packages as shared pure function, both find_package_files and find_package_files_with_context now use it.

title: Consider 'which' crate for command availability checks
description: ShellCommandRunner::is_command_available spawns a shell process to run 'command -v'. The 'which' crate can do this natively without spawning a process — faster and avoids shell-related edge cases. Would also eliminate the default timeout wait (60s) for simple availability checks.
close_reason: Replaced shell-based is_command_available with which crate for native PATH lookup

title: PackageParseError::FileSystemError erases source error to String
description: PackageParseError::FileSystemError converts the source FileSystemError to a String (source_message: String), losing the error chain. Other error types in the codebase preserve #[source] for proper error chain propagation. This variant should store the original error or at least an Arc<FileSystemError> to maintain the chain.
close_reason: Replaced source_message: String with #[source] source: Arc<FileSystemError> to preserve error chain

title: Package pub(crate) fields accessed inconsistently — direct access vs accessors
description: Package has pub(crate) fields with accessor methods, but internal code inconsistently uses direct field access (e.g., package.name, package.environments) vs the public accessor methods (e.g., package.name(), package.environments()). Should standardize to always use accessors, then tighten field visibility.
close_reason: GetPackage fields are now pub(crate) with consistent accessor methods; CLI uses accessors everywhere

title: Emoji handling inconsistent — install.rs hard-codes emoji outside TerminalProgressReporter
description: Most emoji/styling goes through TerminalProgressReporter, but install.rs hard-codes 📦 and 🔧 directly in InstallationDisplay::add_output_line. All emoji should be handled consistently through TerminalProgressReporter to respect --no-color and terminal capability detection.
close_reason: Routed all emoji in install.rs through TerminalProgressReporter with proper console::Emoji fallbacks and use_colors support

title: Replace unsafe NonZeroU64::new_unchecked with safe const
description: config.rs:50 and config.rs:64 use unsafe { NonZeroU64::new_unchecked(60) } and unsafe { NonZeroUsize::new_unchecked(4) } for compile-time constants. Since Rust 1.83, these can be replaced with safe const blocks: const { NonZeroU64::new(60).unwrap() } which fails at compile time if zero is passed. No reason to use unsafe here.
close_reason: Replaced unsafe NonZero with safe const blocks

title: Fix typos: ApplyToConfg and SUGGESTION_EJOJI
description: Two naming typos in the codebase: (1) ApplyToConfg trait in config/loader.rs is missing an 'i' — should be ApplyToConfig. Used in loader.rs, main.rs, and cli/config.rs. (2) SUGGESTION_EJOJI constant in terminal_progress_reporter.rs should be SUGGESTION_EMOJI.
close_reason: Renamed ApplyToConfg→ApplyToConfig (4 files) and SUGGESTION_EJOJI→SUGGESTION_EMOJI (1 file). All checks pass.

title: Extract handle_missing_environment to steps.rs (DRY)
description: handle_missing_environment is duplicated verbatim in check.rs:123 and install.rs:328. The error construction and event sending are identical; only the return type differs. This should be extracted to steps.rs as a shared function.
close_reason: Extracted handle_missing_environment to steps.rs with generic <T>, removed Box::new+deref anti-pattern in handle_missing_check_command, made function sync instead of needlessly async

title: Address verbose/use_colors in library AppConfig
description: AppConfig contains verbose and use_colors fields which are purely presentation concerns -- the library doesn't use them for any logic. They exist solely so the CLI can read them back out after loading config. Options: (1) split into CoreConfig + UI config, (2) document that these are consumed by UI layers. Either way, clarify the boundary for v1.
close_reason: Split AppConfig into SelfieConfig (library) and CliConfig (CLI). Library no longer contains verbose/use_colors. Config file supports sectioned format with cli: section.

title: Unify PackageService method return types
description: Some service methods return EventStream directly (check, install) while others return Result<EventStream, PackageError> (info, validate, list, create). The Result wrapper on the latter group adds nothing since the inner call never fails -- they all wrap with Ok(self.execute_operation_with_deps(...)). Pick one approach for API consistency before v1.
close_reason: Already implemented — all PackageService methods now uniformly return EventStream directly

title: truncate_stderr has a narrower name than the concept it enforces
description:
crates/selfie/src/commands/runner.rs defines truncate_stderr, called from two places that do the same real job but with different inputs:
  - resolve.rs:256 and event.rs:1278/1720 pass actual stderr bytes.
  - resolve.rs:251 passes e.to_string() — an ERROR MESSAGE, not stderr.

Both are bounding text selfie does not control before it enters a diagnostic. The name describes only one of them, which will mislead the next person deciding whether a third call site is appropriate: someone with untrusted text that is not stderr may conclude the function does not apply and invent a second bound, which is exactly what selfie-ppp consolidated away.

Cheap fix: rename to something naming the concept rather than the field — truncate_forwarded or bound_untrusted_text — and reword the doc comment to match. Both existing call sites then read correctly. MAX_STDERR_BYTES can keep its name or follow.

Out of scope for selfie-ppp: pre-existing, and a rename touching the credential path should not ride a documentation amendment. Note selfie-iuhz also concerns this function (a rule mandates it that one site violates and two crates cannot call it) — worth doing together, since that one may change its visibility anyway.
acceptance_criteria: The function's name describes the concept it enforces, so a caller with non-stderr untrusted text recognizes it applies.

title: CLAUDE.md's cargo test -p selfie note reads as present tense and cites a closed bead
description:
CLAUDE.md's gate-commands section ends the second bullet with: 'The command genuinely did not compile before PR #67; selfie-4b7 tracks that.'

Two problems, both small, one demonstrated.

1. It caused a real misread. During the P1/P2 batch a careful agent read that bullet and reported to the lead that 'CLAUDE.md still documents cargo test -p selfie as not compiling' and that the note was stale — on a branch where the corrected text was already present. It had parsed the past-tense clause as a present-tense claim. The lead checked and found the report false. Documentation that leads a competent reader to the opposite conclusion is a defect regardless of whether the sentence is literally true.

2. 'selfie-4b7 tracks that' is now false. selfie-4b7 was closed when PR #70 merged. A closed bead tracks nothing, and pointing a reader at it invites them to reopen a resolved question.

Fix: either drop the trailing sentence (the bullet's job — do not remove the test-common feature line — is complete without it), or reword so the tense is unmistakable and the citation is historical rather than active, e.g. 'Before PR #67 this command did not compile at all; that is why the older instructions prescribed a feature flag.'

Filed rather than fixed inline because the batch's units were scoped to other files.
acceptance_criteria: The note cannot be read as claiming the command currently fails, and does not cite a closed issue as active.
close_reason:
Fixed in PR #73 (merged d9bb7f9).

selfie-blkr: the pre-commit-check skill was DELETED rather than corrected. It duplicated a checklist CLAUDE.md already carries and already loads every session, and that duplication is what let the two drift apart. CLAUDE.md's checklist now delegates to 'just check', so no second copy of the commands exists to weaken. Premise verified empirically rather than restated: on an isolated copy with a planted clippy::needless_return, 'cargo clippy --all-targets' exits 0 while printing the warning and '-- -D warnings' exits 101 on identical code.

selfie-it6l: resolved differently than the bead framed it. The question assumed a hand-picked crate+feature invocation was the right instrument. selfie is the only crate in the workspace with an optional feature (with_mocks; mockall is the only optional=true dependency), so it was the only crate worth isolating and nothing said why. CI now runs 'cargo hack --each-feature test -p selfie', covering all four combinations instead of the one the workspace run produces, and extending itself if a second feature appears. Removed from the local checklist: the break can only reach main through a PR, and CI gates PRs. Verified the replacement is a strict superset — deleting test-common's features line fails cargo-hack on pass 2 of 4 with the predicted from_parts error, and the old gate exits 101 on the same mutation.

selfie-cm1h: the trailing sentence was retensed and its citation historicized rather than deleted, so it still explains why obsolete '--features with_mocks' instructions exist elsewhere. Worth recording why this was more than a P4 nit: THREE independent agents misread that sentence during this batch — one reported CLAUDE.md as stale, one claimed 'just test-lib' would fail every time and cited it as proof, one filed it as a stale-docs finding on an unrelated PR. All three were wrong. The mechanism, diagnosed by the selfie-ppp author, is that all three misread a TRAILING CLAUSE qualifying an earlier claim; a reader who stops at the first assertion gets the opposite meaning. The fix leads with 'The command compiles today.' as a standalone sentence.

title: Five doc comments describe behavior the code does not have
description:
Found by a comment-accuracy sweep of the provider-sourced dotfiles change. Each is a comment stating something checkable that turns out not to hold. Grouped because it is one pass, not five investigations; each is a few lines.

1. crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/port.rs:32 — ConflictDetail::Diff says the diff 'may be empty if the files are binary or unreadable'. unified_diff returns empty on exactly one condition, the two sides being identical (dotfile_service/diff.rs:15), which the conflict path excludes by construction. An unreadable or non-UTF-8 target becomes an empty string and diffs as a FULL ADDITION — the largest possible diff, not an empty one. Both named causes produce the opposite of the documented effect.

2. crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:570 — the comment justifying the extra candidate in report_apply_time_commands says the shared set 'is the effective set for an environment that declares no dotfiles of its own, so it is a candidate in its own right'. That case is already covered by the preceding map, since such an environment is still a key in environments(). The chain is actually load-bearing for a case the comment does not name: a package with an EMPTY environments map, where max() over the mapped iterator is None and the notice vanishes. Not hypothetical — handle_track_standalone builds specs with no environments, so a standalone dotfile spec with a command entry depends on that line.

3. crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/resolve.rs:234 — run_capture is documented as 'returning stdout, or stderr on failure'. Only the non-zero-exit branch returns stderr; the Err(CommandError) branch returns the error's Display ('Command timed out after 30s: …'). That lands in ResolveError::CommandFailed { stderr }, whose type doc says every variant carries 'stderr, which is forwarded on failure only'. No leak, but the field does not hold what two comments say.

4. crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/resolve.rs:112 — check_resolvable says a preview 'declines exactly what a real apply declines'. It declines one thing, a template path escaping the package directory. A real apply additionally declines an unreadable template, empty provider output, an empty binding, a failing command and oversized content. The doc's own first line bounds the scope correctly, so 'exactly' contradicts it two lines later.

5. crates/selfie/src/package/port.rs:73 — read_referenced_file's # Errors lists only 'the file does not exist, cannot be read, or is not valid UTF-8'. The implementation also returns PermissionDenied for a path escaping the package directory — the containment refusal that is the whole reason this method lives on the repository rather than being a plain read.

Also pre-existing, same failure mode, in a file this work touched: crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:235 has two doc comments welded together, four lines describing expand_user_path above the actual is_safe_name summary.
acceptance_criteria: Each comment describes what its code does, verified rather than assumed.

title: template_dotfiles iterates a HashMap, so validation output order is nondeterministic
description:
crates/selfie/src/package/validate.rs:614 walks self.environments(), a HashMap<String, EnvironmentConfig>, without sorting. Its sibling dotfiles_with_scope sorts environment names explicitly for this reason (crates/selfie/src/package.rs:578), and the same change added a sort to list_yaml_files with a comment about ext4 hash order versus APFS. template_dotfiles missed it.

Reproduce with a package declaring dotfiles under two environments, each a template with a declared-but-unused var: 'selfie spec validate' emits the two errors in a per-process-random relative order, and so do validate --all and the MCP issues array.

Cosmetic in effect — the same issues are reported either way — but it makes output diffs and any test asserting on issue order unstable, which is the class of problem the list_yaml_files sort was added to prevent.

Package::validate_dotfiles has the same shape at validate.rs:519 but predates this work.
acceptance_criteria: Validation reports issues in a deterministic order regardless of filesystem or hash iteration order.

title: Consolidate the duplicated fake CommandRunner into the selfie crate
description:
Two identical hand-rolled fake command runners exist: FakeRunner in crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/resolve.rs (unit tests) and FakeCommandRunner in crates/test-common/src/runner.rs (integration tests, 195 lines). Both return canned responses per command and record the calls they received.

The comment at resolve.rs:288-296 explains the duplication as forced, and it is right about the direction it tested: test-common depends on selfie, so importing test-common into a selfie unit test links a second copy of the lib and its FakeCommandRunner implements a different CommandRunner trait than the one in scope.

But the dependency runs one way, so the inverse works. Move the fake into selfie behind #[cfg(any(test, feature = "with_mocks"))] — the gate MockCommandRunner already uses at commands/runner.rs:47 — and have test-common re-export it, which it already does for other selfie types at lib.rs:39. Then selfie's unit tests use it directly with no cycle, and integration tests get the same type through test-common.

Two things not to fold in. ConcurrencyTrackingRunner (package/service/list.rs:265) looks similar but measures peak parallelism by incrementing an atomic and sleeping rather than returning responses; merging it would produce a double with two unrelated jobs. And MockCommandRunner stays for the cases that need neither recording nor Clone.

Also update or remove the resolve.rs comment, which currently asserts the consolidation is impossible rather than impossible in one direction.
acceptance_criteria: One fake CommandRunner serves both unit and integration tests; the resolve.rs comment matches what is actually true.
notes: Raised by the user reviewing PR #67. The comment's claim was verified in the direction it was tested and stated more broadly than the evidence supported.

title: Resolved secrets are not erasable from process memory
description:
Dotfile provider content lives in String and Vec buffers that Rust may reallocate, leaving copies behind, so selfie makes no scrubbing guarantee. The conflict path holds a second copy while consulting the resolver, since the values must outlive the spawn_blocking call that presents them.

Documented in docs/package-files.md rather than claimed to be handled. Filed so the option is evaluated deliberately rather than assumed impossible: zeroize on the final buffer is cheap and worth something, but it must not be described as a guarantee it cannot make — a partial scrub that reads as complete is worse than an honest limitation.
acceptance_criteria: Either secret buffers are zeroed where it is meaningful, or the limitation is a recorded decision rather than an untested assumption.

title: Whether an in-sync symlinked secret target is replaced depends on its destination mode
description:
is_owner_only uses fs::metadata, which follows symlinks. So for a secret target that is a symlink and already in sync: if the destination is 0644 the target is tightened, and write_file_private replaces the link with a regular file; if the destination is already 0600 the entry is skipped and the link survives.

Replacing is consistent with the documented behavior that a symlink at the target is replaced rather than written through. The conditionality is what is new and undocumented — the same entry behaves differently depending on a mode the user may not have looked at.

Narrow, and arguably the better behavior in both directions. Filed to document rather than to change.
acceptance_criteria: The symlink behavior of an in-sync secret target is documented, or made unconditional.

title: unreachable! in the sync push validation gate
description:
crates/selfie/src/sync_service/service.rs:670 uses unreachable!() for the Info arm of the validation-level match. It is genuinely unreachable — a positive filter six lines above admits only Error and Warning — and the arm is kept so that adding a level is a compile error rather than a silent reclassification, which is the property that match was rewritten to establish.

The cost is that a future edit to that filter turns a mislabeled issue into a process abort during sync push. A filter_map returning None for Info would keep the exhaustiveness, and hence the build failure on a new variant, without the panic.

Cosmetic against current code; filed so the trade-off is recorded rather than rediscovered.
acceptance_criteria: The push gate cannot panic on a validation level, and a new level still fails the build.

title: Dry run still prompts for repo-file conflicts before discovering it will do nothing
description: crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:996-1017: with --dry-run, a repository-file conflict still invokes the interactive resolver, so the user is asked to decide about an overwrite that will not happen. The secret-bearing path was fixed to check dry_run first; the repository-file path was not, leaving the two inconsistent within the same function.
acceptance_criteria: A dry run prompts for nothing.

title: dotfiles list and selfie_dotfiles_list bypass the service layer
description:
crates/mcp-server/src/server.rs and the CLI's dotfiles list handler call PackageRepository::list_packages directly. CLAUDE.md states that CLI and MCP commands should call SpecService or PackageService methods rather than using PackageRepository directly.

Pre-existing, and framed in the code as the same deliberate 'bypass the service layer for fast file reads' pattern used by spec list. Provider-sourced dotfiles extended the bypass: the new content-source rendering for these two commands is never seen by the service layer, so no service-level test covers what they report.

Either route them through a service, or record the bypass as a sanctioned exception in CLAUDE.md so it stops reading as drift.
acceptance_criteria: Either these commands go through a service, or the exception is documented as intentional.

title: MockFileSystem and MockCommandRunner use inconsistent feature gates
description:
crates/selfie/src/fs/filesystem.rs:21 gates the FileSystem automock on feature = "with_mocks" alone, while crates/selfie/src/commands/runner.rs:47 gates CommandRunner's on any(test, feature = "with_mocks"). The crate's own tests therefore get one mock but not the other, which is the direct cause of selfie-4b7 (cargo test -p selfie failing to compile without the feature).

Making the gates consistent likely resolves selfie-4b7 outright.
acceptance_criteria: Both mocks use the same gate; cargo test -p selfie compiles without extra flags.

title: sync status counts provider-sourced dotfiles it never verifies
description:
crates/selfie/src/dotfile_service/service.rs:768 increments total_count before the content_source() match, so once secret-bearing entries are skipped during drift checking they still contribute to the 'N dotfiles' total that sync status reports via total_deployed (crates/selfie/src/sync_service/service.rs:900-910).

Cosmetic rather than incorrect, but it overstates what has actually been verified — the total implies a check that did not happen for those entries.
acceptance_criteria: Totals reported by sync status distinguish verified entries from entries that cannot be verified.

title: Confirm the temp-location test actually exercises its assertion on CI
description:
crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs, test creates_the_temporary_file_in_the_targets_own_directory. It pins write_file_private to creating its temp file in the target's own directory — the property that makes the rename atomic — and is the only test that would catch that being changed to a plain temp-dir location.

It can only discriminate when the target and $TMPDIR are on different filesystems, so it creates its target under /dev/shm and self-skips when the device check does not hold. It is #[cfg(target_os = "linux")], so it never runs on macOS.

CI confirms it runs on Linux (13 tests there vs 12 on macOS) but not that it did anything: an early return reports 'ok' exactly like a real pass. The test prints a skip marker via eprintln!, which plain 'cargo test' captures and shows only for failures.

To resolve: run 'cargo test -p selfie --features with_mocks private_write_tests -- --nocapture' on a Linux machine and look for a SKIP line. If it skips there too, the test has never asserted anything anywhere and should either be reworked or removed rather than left as apparent coverage.
acceptance_criteria: It is known whether the test exercises its assertion on CI; if it does not, it is reworked or removed.

title: write_file and write_file_private handle an empty parent path differently
description:
RealFileSystem::write_file (crates/selfie/src/fs/real.rs:22-29) calls create_dir_all(path.parent()) without the empty-path filter that write_file_private applies. Path::new("creds").parent() is Some(""), not None, so the two sibling methods now treat the same input via different code.

Harmless today — std special-cases create_dir_all("") to Ok and an empty base joins to the original path — so this is readability rather than a defect. But two adjacent methods handling identical input differently reads as a bug to the next person, and invites someone to 'fix' the wrong one.
acceptance_criteria: Both methods derive the parent directory the same way, or a comment explains why they differ.

title: Investigate TOML as alternative config format
description: TOML is the Rust ecosystem standard (Cargo.toml). Evaluate whether it would be a better fit than YAML for selfie package specs. Consider: first-class Rust serde support, familiarity for Rust users, handling of nested structures (environments with commands/deps), comments support, no type coercion footguns. Main concern: TOML can be verbose for deeply nested structures like per-environment install/check commands with dependencies.

title: Investigate Nickel as alternative config format
description: Nickel (nickel-lang.org) is a configuration language written in Rust with gradual typing and contracts. Evaluate whether it would be a better fit than YAML for selfie package specs. Consider: Rust-native (no external runtime), built-in validation via contracts, human-readability for hand-edited files, learning curve for users, ecosystem maturity, serde integration story. Compare with current YAML + serde-saphyr + garde approach.

title: Use spawn_blocking for git CLI calls in async tasks
description: Copilot review flagged that execute_push and pull call synchronous git CLI commands (stage_files, commit, push, fetch, fast_forward) inside tokio async tasks. This can block worker threads during long network ops. Consider wrapping blocking git calls in tokio::task::spawn_blocking, or making the git provider trait async. Low priority — selfie is a personal CLI tool, so thread starvation is unlikely in practice.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add version field to package specs
description: Add an optional version field to package spec files for tracking which version of a package definition the user has. This is about the spec version, not the installed package version. Found in selfie-v3 old repo.
close_reason: User decided against this — version field was recently removed intentionally

title: Graceful shutdown on SIGINT/SIGTERM during installs
description: Handle SIGINT/SIGTERM signals gracefully during long-running install operations. Should clean up any in-progress state and exit cleanly rather than leaving partial installations. Found as planned (but not implemented) in selfie-v3 old repo.
close_reason: Added SIGTERM handling alongside existing SIGINT, plus user-facing cancellation message

title: Add file logging with rotation support
description: Add optional file logging with configuration for log directory, max files, and max file size. Useful for debugging issues after the fact. The old selfie-v3 repo had --log-enable, --log-directory, --log-max-files, --log-max-size flags. Current repo uses tracing but has no file logging configuration.

title: Move collect_all_packages inside spawned task for immediate stream return
description: collect_all_packages() currently runs before create_event_stream(), which delays the Started event and blocks the caller while parsing YAML files. Moving package collection inside the spawned task would let the stream return immediately. Low priority for typical workloads (~50 YAML files) but would improve responsiveness for large repos. Flagged by Copilot review on PR #33.

title: JoinError emits PackageListItem with empty version and environments
description: In service/list.rs:160, on JoinError the emitted PackageListItem uses an empty version and environments. The CLI list renderer formats 'v{version}', so this displays as just 'v' with no environment context. Since the original package metadata is available from PackageListReady, the error completion item should preserve at least version and environments while setting status = Error(...).
close_reason: JoinError metadata fix and ErrorCollector wiring implemented

title: Route list command summary through DisplayManager
description: P4: The summary at the end of list (list.rs:215-234) uses bare println\! for 'Package directory: ...' and count summaries. Will break when Phase 2 spinners arrive. Also uses no symbols/colors for summary counts, making it visually flat. Route through DisplayManager for consistency.
close_reason: list.rs summary already routed through DisplayManager in 8d1 (PR #23)

title: Deduplicate spinner initialization code
description: P4: start_operation and start_list_spinner (display_manager.rs:365-417) are identical except for max_output_lines: 5 vs 0. Should be a single method with a parameter or a builder pattern.
close_reason: Implemented in commit a8ac5ff on feat/cli-display-consistency branch

title: Add human-panic crate — friendly panic messages (CLI only)
description:
Add human_panic::setup_panic!() as the first line in main() (crates/cli/src/main.rs). Replaces raw stack traces with user-friendly crash report files.

Effort: Minimal — one line + one dep in CLI Cargo.toml.
close_reason: Closed

title: Evaluate 'tabled' crate for derive-macro table formatting
description: tables.rs manually builds tables with comfy-table. The 'tabled' crate offers derive macros for table formatting directly from structs, which could reduce the manual table-building code. Evaluate whether switching or using tabled would simplify output formatting.

title: Consider 'indicatif' crate for progress display
description:
indicatif is by mitsuhiko (same author as console crate already in use), ensuring compatibility. Would only be used in CLI crate (library boundary rule preserved). Current progress is text-only emoji prefixes via TerminalProgressReporter and ProgressTracker; indicatif adds spinners, progress bars, and MultiProgress for future parallel installs.

Evaluate whether indicatif would simplify the current progress code and improve UX for long-running operations like package installation.
close_reason: Phase 1 complete: replaced TerminalProgressReporter with indicatif-powered DisplayManager. PR #16 targets uat branch. Phase 2 (wiring spinners into event handlers) can be a follow-up issue.

title: PackageRepoError boxing requires manual Box::new at every error site
description: PackageRepoError::PackageError(Box<PackageError>) requires callers to write Box::new(PackageError::Foo { .. }).into() at every error site. A From<PackageError> for PackageRepoError impl that auto-boxes would be cleaner and reduce boilerplate.
close_reason: Added From<PackageError> for PackageRepoError impl and simplified all call sites

title: TerminalProgressReporter methods inconsistently take self vs &self
description: TerminalProgressReporter is a Copy struct (contains only a bool), but its methods inconsistently take self (consuming Copy) vs &self (borrowing). While harmless for Copy types, it's visually inconsistent and should be standardized to &self throughout.
close_reason: Closed

title: Clean up dead test helpers in test-common
description: Several fixture functions in test-common/src/fixtures.rs are defined but never imported or used by any test file: create_multi_env_package_file, create_incomplete_package_file, create_custom_package_file, create_failing_package_file, and create_slow_package_file. These should be removed to keep the test infrastructure lean.
close_reason: Removed 5 dead fixture functions from test-common/fixtures.rs (create_multi_env_package_file, create_incomplete_package_file, create_custom_package_file, create_failing_package_file, create_slow_package_file). Committed in 5202d84.

title: Remove async_trait from synchronous FileSystem trait
description: filesystem.rs:22 applies #[async_trait::async_trait] to the FileSystem trait, but all methods are synchronous fn, not async fn. The macro is misleading and unnecessary. It should be removed.
close_reason: Removed #[async_trait::async_trait] from FileSystem trait. All methods were synchronous; the macro was misleading and unnecessary.
